```{julia}
using ForwardDiff   # explicit gradients for Optim (autodiff kwarg pipeline broken in current Optim)

# PrettyTables v3 compatibility shim. v3 dropped `ft_printf` (now
# `fmt__printf`) and requires the `formatters` keyword to be a Vector.
# All call sites in this document use the v2 form
# `formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf(fmt, cols)`; re-create
# `ft_printf` so it returns a single-element Vector wrapping the new
# `fmt__printf`, accepting either an Int column index or a range.
if !isdefined(PrettyTables, :ft_printf)
    @eval PrettyTables begin
        ft_printf(fmt, cols) =
            [fmt__printf(fmt, collect(cols isa Integer ? (cols:cols) : cols))]
        ft_printf(fmt) = [fmt__printf(fmt)]   # apply to all columns (v2 single-arg)
    end
end

# PrettyTables v3 also renamed the `header` keyword to `column_labels`
# (which must be an `AbstractVector` — a flat vector for one header row,
# or a vector of row-vectors for stacked headers; a Tuple is rejected).
# `_pt_compat` wraps `pretty_table` so the document's v2-style calls keep
# working: it maps `header` → `column_labels` (Tuple → Vector), and
# normalises `formatters` to a flat Vector. All `PrettyTables.pretty_table`
# call sites in the document route through this wrapper. `_PT_REAL` holds
# the real function (no trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves
# it untouched — no recursion).
const _PT_REAL = PrettyTables.pretty_table
function _pt_compat(data; header = nothing, formatters = nothing,
                    body_hlines = nothing, kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    if header !== nothing
        kw[:column_labels] = header isa Tuple ? collect(header) : header
    end
    if formatters !== nothing
        kw[:formatters] =
            formatters isa Function ? [formatters] :
            formatters isa Tuple ?
                collect(Iterators.flatten(
                    x isa Union{AbstractVector,Tuple} ? x : (x,) for x in formatters)) :
                formatters
    end
    # `body_hlines` (v2) has no v3 equivalent — it only drew cosmetic
    # horizontal rules after given rows. Captured here and dropped so the
    # table still renders (without the extra separators). `alignment` and
    # `row_labels` are unchanged in v3 and pass straight through.
    return _PT_REAL(data; kw...)
end

# Optim autodiff compat shim. The installed Optim's `autodiff` kwarg
# rejects the Symbol form `:forward` (it now expects an ADTypes type),
# and even the ADTypes path trips a DifferentiationInterface bug in
# this version. The fix: don't use Optim's autodiff plumbing at all —
# wrap `f` with an explicit ForwardDiff-computed gradient and call the
# 5-arg `optimize(f, g!, x0, method, opts)` form, which doesn't go
# through autodiff. `_optimize_compat` routes every Optim.optimize call
# in the document through this translation; 4-arg calls with
# `autodiff = :forward` are rewritten to the 5-arg gradient form, all
# other shapes pass through. `_OPT_REAL` holds the real function (no
# trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves it untouched).
const _OPT_REAL = Optim.optimize
function _optimize_compat(args...; kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    ad = pop!(kw, :autodiff, nothing)
    # If `autodiff = :forward` is requested, build the gradient via
    # ForwardDiff and use the explicit-gradient path. Handles any arg
    # shape where args[1]=f, args[2]=x0 (method/options follow): 3-arg
    # `(f, x0, method)`, 4-arg `(f, x0, method, opts)`, etc.
    if ad isa Symbol && (ad === :forward || ad === :forwarddiff) && length(args) >= 2
        f, x0 = args[1], args[2]
        g!(g, x) = ForwardDiff.gradient!(g, f, x)
        return _OPT_REAL(f, g!, x0, args[3:end]...; kw...)
    end
    return ad === nothing ? _OPT_REAL(args...; kw...) :
                            _OPT_REAL(args...; autodiff = ad, kw...)
end
```

```{julia}
_rawval(x) = hasproperty(x, :value) ? x.value : x  # unwrap ReadStatTables.LabeledValue

function _numeric_vec(col)
    vals = collect(skipmissing(col))
    isempty(vals) && return Float64[]
    T = Base.nonmissingtype(eltype(col))
    T <: Real && return convert(Vector{Float64}, vals)
    try
        return Float64[Float64(_rawval(v)) for v in vals]
    catch
        return nothing  # non-numeric (strings, etc.)
    end
end

"""
Expand a Stata-style varlist pattern against DataFrame columns. Supports:
  * `t*`, `*t`, `*mpg*`, `t?`   — glob wildcards
  * `price-weight`              — range of columns (inclusive, by column order)
  * exact names, Symbols, vectors, and the literal "_all"
"""
function _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    cols = string.(DataFrames.names(df))
    patterns = vars isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [string(vars)] :
               vars isa AbstractVector ? [string(v) for v in vars] :
               [string(v) for v in collect(vars)]

    out = String[]
    for p in patterns
        if p == "_all"
            append!(out, cols)
        elseif occursin('*', p) || occursin('?', p)
            rx = Regex("^" * replace(p, "*" => ".*", "?" => ".") * "\$")
            for c in cols
                occursin(rx, c) && push!(out, c)
            end
        elseif occursin('-', p) && !startswith(p, "-") && !(p in cols)
            parts = split(p, '-', limit=2)
            i = findfirst(==(String(parts[1])), cols)
            j = findfirst(==(String(parts[2])), cols)
            (i === nothing || j === nothing) && error("Unknown variable in range '$p'")
            i, j = minmax(i, j)
            append!(out, cols[i:j])
        else
            push!(out, p)
        end
    end

    seen = Set{String}(); uniq = String[]
    for v in out
        v in seen || (push!(seen, v); push!(uniq, v))
    end
    return Symbol.(uniq)
end

function summarize_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, vars=nothing; detail::Bool=false)
    if vars === nothing
        varlist = Symbol[]
        for n in DataFrames.names(df)
            _numeric_vec(df[!, n]) === nothing || push!(varlist, Symbol(n))
        end
    else
        varlist = _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    end

    rows = []
    for v in varlist
        xraw = _numeric_vec(df[!, v])
        x = xraw === nothing ? Float64[] : xraw
        n = length(x)
        if n == 0
            push!(rows, (; Variable=string(v), Obs=0, Mean=missing,
                           Std=missing, Min=missing, Max=missing))
            continue
        end
        μ  = Statistics.mean(x)
        σ  = n > 1 ? Statistics.std(x) : missing
        base = (; Variable=string(v), Obs=n, Mean=μ, Std=σ,
                  Min=minimum(x), Max=maximum(x))
        if detail
            qs = Statistics.quantile(x, [0.01,0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50,0.75,0.90,0.95,0.99])
            # Stata uses biased moments for skewness/kurtosis
            m2 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^2)
            m3 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^3)
            m4 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^4)
            skew = m2 > 0 ? m3 / m2^(3/2) : missing
            kurt = m2 > 0 ? m4 / m2^2     : missing
            push!(rows, merge(base,
                (; p1=qs[1], p5=qs[2], p10=qs[3], p25=qs[4], p50=qs[5],
                   p75=qs[6], p90=qs[7], p95=qs[8], p99=qs[9],
                   Variance = ismissing(σ) ? missing : σ^2,
                   Skewness = skew, Kurtosis = kurt)))
        else
            push!(rows, base)
        end
    end

    # Stata's `summarize, detail` block — one per requested variable.
    if detail
        _g9d(x; w::Int = 9, mx::Int = 7) = begin
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
            sig = mx
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            while length(s) > w && sig > 1
                sig -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
        end
        _comma_d(n::Integer) = replace(string(n), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
        for r in rows
            v = r.Variable
            x = _numeric_vec(df[!, Symbol(v)])
            x === nothing && (println("$v: not numeric"); continue)
            n = length(x); ssorted = sort(x)
            small4 = ssorted[1:min(4, n)]
            large4 = ssorted[max(1, n - 3):n]    # ascending; Stata also shows ascending here
            println()
            println(lpad(v, 36))
            println("-"^61)
            println(lpad("Percentiles", 26),  lpad("Smallest", 16))
            pct = [0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99]
            qs  = Statistics.quantile(x, pct)
            sml = [get(small4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            lrg = [get(large4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            # Row 1: 1% / small[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "1%",
                           _g9d(qs[1]), _g9d(sml[1]))
            # Row 2: 5% / small[2]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "5%",
                           _g9d(qs[2]), _g9d(sml[2]))
            # Row 3: 10% / small[3]                Obs <N>
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "10%",
                           _g9d(qs[3]), _g9d(sml[3]),
                           "Obs", _comma_d(n))
            # Row 4: 25% / small[4]                Sum of wgt.
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "25%",
                           _g9d(qs[4]), _g9d(sml[4]),
                           "Sum of wgt.", _comma_d(n))
            println()
            # Row 5: 50% / blank          Mean
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "50%",
                           _g9d(qs[5]), "", "Mean", _g9d(r.Mean))
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n",
                           "", "", "Largest",
                           "Std. dev.", _g9d(r.Std))
            # Row 6: 75% / large[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "75%",
                           _g9d(qs[6]), _g9d(lrg[1]))
            println()
            # Row 7: 90% / large[2]                Variance
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "90%",
                           _g9d(qs[7]), _g9d(lrg[2]),
                           "Variance", _g9d(r.Variance))
            # Row 8: 95% / large[3]                Skewness
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "95%",
                           _g9d(qs[8]), _g9d(lrg[3]),
                           "Skewness", _g9d(r.Skewness))
            # Row 9: 99% / large[4]                Kurtosis
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "99%",
                           _g9d(qs[9]), _g9d(lrg[4]),
                           "Kurtosis", _g9d(r.Kurtosis))
        end
        return
    end

    # Stata %9.0g: up to 7 sig figs, capped at 9 chars total (so leading "0."
    # for |x|<1 fits), then leading "0" stripped from |x|<1.
    _g9(x; w::Int=9, mx::Int=7) = begin
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
        sig = mx
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        while length(s) > w && sig > 1
            sig -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
    end
    _comma(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    println("    Variable |        Obs        Mean    Std. dev.       Min        Max")
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^57)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |  %9s   %9s   %9s  %9s  %9s\n",
                       r.Variable, _comma(r.Obs),
                       _g9(r.Mean), _g9(r.Std),
                       _g9(r.Min),  _g9(r.Max))
    end
end

"""
    test_stata(model, vars; values=zeros(length(vars)), depvar="docvis", V=nothing)
    test_stata(model; restrictions, depvar="docvis", V=nothing)

Stata-style `test` for ML-based estimators (Poisson, logit, …). Two call
forms:

1. **Simple form** — pass coef name(s) and (optionally) RHS values. Each
   variable is tested = its `values[k]` (default 0). Equivalent to Stata's
   `test female` / `test female private`.

2. **Joint linear-restrictions form** — pass `restrictions = [r1, r2, …]`
   where each `r_i` is a `Pair{Vector{Pair}, Number}` (use a Vector — not a
   Dict — so display ordering is deterministic). Example:

       ["female" => 1.0]                    => 0.0   #  female = 0
       ["private" => 1.0, "chronic" => 1.0] => 1.0   #  private + chronic = 1

   The LHS vector lists `coefname => weight` pairs in the order they should
   appear in the printed equation; the pair value is the RHS. Equivalent to
   Stata's `test (female) (private + chronic = 1)`. Display strings are
   auto-generated to match Stata's exact format (`[depvar]name`, sign-aware
   coefficients, `+`/`-` joiners).

`V` overrides `vcov(model)` — pass the robust V from `poisson_stata` /
`setup_mus10().V_robust` to match Stata's `test` after `vce(robust)`.
"""
function test_stata(model=nothing, vars=nothing; values=nothing,
                    depvar::AbstractString="docvis",
                    V=nothing, restrictions=nothing,
                    mtest::Bool=false,
                    β=nothing, coefnames=nothing)
    # `β`, `V`, `coefnames` overrides let you test NB / GMM / quantile-
    # regression / bootstrap-derived coefficients without a Stata-style
    # model object — pass `model = nothing`. The first non-nothing source
    # for β / V / coefnames is used (so `test_stata(model)` still works).
    β     = β === nothing ? StatsBase.coef(model) : collect(β)
    Vmat  = V === nothing ? Matrix(StatsBase.vcov(model)) : Matrix(V)
    names = coefnames === nothing ? string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model)) :
                                    string.(coefnames)
    p_idx(v) = (i = findfirst(==(string(v)), names);
                i === nothing && error("'$(v)' not in coefnames=$(names)");
                i)

    # Build R (q × k), r (q-vector), and a display label for each restriction.
    # The LHS of each restriction is a Vector of `coefname => weight` pairs
    # (we accept Dict too for convenience, but ordering is unspecified).
    if restrictions !== nothing
        q = length(restrictions); k = length(β)
        R = zeros(q, k); r = zeros(q); labels = String[]
        for (row, restr) in enumerate(restrictions)
            coefs, rhs = restr.first, restr.second
            pairs = coefs isa AbstractDict ? collect(coefs) : collect(coefs)
            # Build display terms with Stata-style sign handling:
            #   first positive  →  "[depvar]name"
            #   first negative  →  "- [depvar]name"   (space after `-`)
            #   later positive  →  "+ [depvar]name"
            #   later negative  →  "- [depvar]name"
            # Coefficients with |c| ≠ 1 get a "c*" prefix on the symbol.
            term_strs = String[]
            for (idx, (vname, c)) in enumerate(pairs)
                R[row, p_idx(vname)] = float(c)
                cf      = float(c)
                abs_c   = abs(cf)
                core    = abs_c == 1.0 ? "[$depvar]$vname" :
                          Printf.@sprintf("%g*[%s]%s", abs_c, depvar, vname)
                sign_op = cf < 0 ? "-" : "+"
                if idx == 1
                    push!(term_strs, cf < 0 ? "- $core" : core)
                else
                    push!(term_strs, "$sign_op $core")
                end
            end
            r[row] = float(rhs)
            push!(labels, join(term_strs, " ") *
                          " = " * Printf.@sprintf("%g", r[row]))
        end
    else
        vs   = vars isa AbstractVector ? string.(vars) : [string(vars)]
        vals = values === nothing ? zeros(length(vs)) : collect(values)
        q = length(vs); k = length(β)
        R = zeros(q, k); r = vals
        labels = String[]
        # When `depvar` is empty (e.g. testing differences from a bootstrap
        # of an estimator without a single dependent variable), omit the
        # `[depvar]` prefix entirely — matches Stata's behavior for tests
        # on stored vectors with no equation label.
        for (row, v) in enumerate(vs)
            R[row, p_idx(v)] = 1.0
            prefix = isempty(depvar) ? "" : "[$depvar]"
            push!(labels, "$prefix$v = " * Printf.@sprintf("%g", vals[row]))
        end
    end

    Rβ_r = R * β .- r
    chi2 = (Rβ_r' * (LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(R * Vmat * R') \ Rβ_r))::Float64
    df   = size(R, 1)
    pval = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(df), chi2)
    println()
    for (k_, lab) in enumerate(labels)
        Printf.@printf(" ( %d)  %s\n", k_, lab)
    end
    if mtest
        # `mtest` mode (Stata `test ..., mtest`): each row tested in isolation
        # plus the joint test, in a single table. Default is unadjusted p-values
        # — the matching Stata footnote prints "* Unadjusted p-values".
        chi2_each = [let row = R[i:i, :]; rb = row * β .- r[i:i];
                         (rb' * (LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(row * Vmat * row') \ rb))::Float64
                     end for i in 1:df]
        p_each = [1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(1), c) for c in chi2_each]
        println()
        println("-"^38)
        Printf.@printf("%6s |  %10s  %5s  %9s\n", "", "chi2", "df", "p > chi2")
        println("-"^7, "+", "-"^30)
        for i in 1:df
            Printf.@printf("   (%d) |  %10.2f  %5d  %9.4f*\n",
                           i, chi2_each[i], 1, p_each[i])
        end
        println("-"^7, "+", "-"^30)
        Printf.@printf("%6s |  %10.2f  %5d  %9.4f\n", "All", chi2, df, pval)
        println("-"^38)
        println("* Unadjusted p-values")
    else
        Printf.@printf("\n           chi2(%3d) = %7.2f\n", df, chi2)
        Printf.@printf("         Prob > chi2 = %9.4f\n", pval)
    end
    return (; chi2=chi2, df=df, p=pval)
end

"""
    lrtest_stata(ll_unrestricted, ll_restricted, df)

Stata-style `lrtest` for two nested ML models. Computes
LR = 2·(ll_unr − ll_res), reports `LR chi2(df)` and `Prob > chi2`, with
Stata's "Assumption: restrict nested within unrestrict" header line.

Use after fitting two `*_stata` models (e.g. two `nbreg_stata` calls with
different formulas) and pass the `.ll` fields. `df` is the number of
restrictions (regressors dropped between the unrestricted and restricted
models).
"""
function lrtest_stata(ll_unr::Real, ll_res::Real, df::Int)
    LR = 2 * (Float64(ll_unr) - Float64(ll_res))
    p  = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(df), LR)
    println("Likelihood-ratio test")
    println("Assumption: restrict nested within unrestrict")
    println()
    Printf.@printf(" LR chi2(%d) = %.2f\n", df, LR)
    Printf.@printf("Prob > chi2 = %.4f\n", p)
    return (; LR, df, p)
end

"""
    estat_gof_stata(y, p, g; depvar="", model_label="logistic", quiet=false)
        -> NamedTuple

Stata's `estat gof, group(g)` Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test.
Sorts by predicted probability `p`, partitions into `g` ~equal-sized
groups, then computes
    χ² = Σ_i [(O_{1i} − E_{1i})² / E_{1i} + (O_{0i} − E_{0i})² / E_{0i}]
under H0: model is correctly specified, ~ χ²(g − 2).

When `depvar` is provided, prints Stata's full block:

    Goodness-of-fit test after <model_label> model
    Variable: <depvar>

     Number of observations = …
           Number of groups = …
    Hosmer–Lemeshow chi2(g-2) = …
                Prob > chi2 = …

Returns `(; chi2, df, pvalue, n, g)`.
"""
function estat_gof_stata(y::AbstractVector, p::AbstractVector, g::Int;
                         depvar::AbstractString = "",
                         model_label::AbstractString = "logistic",
                         quiet::Bool = false)
    n   = length(y)
    idx = sortperm(p)
    y_s = y[idx]; p_s = p[idx]
    grp = div(n, g)
    χ2  = 0.0
    for i in 1:g
        lo = (i - 1) * grp + 1
        hi = i == g ? n : i * grp
        ng = hi - lo + 1
        o1 = sum(y_s[lo:hi]); e1 = sum(p_s[lo:hi])
        o0 = ng - o1;          e0 = ng - e1
        e1 > 0 && (χ2 += (o1 - e1)^2 / e1)
        e0 > 0 && (χ2 += (o0 - e0)^2 / e0)
    end
    df = g - 2
    pv = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(df), χ2)
    if !quiet
        commafmt(num) = begin
            s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
            while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
            (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
        end
        if !isempty(depvar)
            println("Goodness-of-fit test after $model_label model")
            println("Variable: $depvar")
            println()
        end
        Printf.@printf("%23s = %7s\n",  "Number of observations", commafmt(n))
        Printf.@printf("%23s = %7d\n",  "Number of groups", g)
        Printf.@printf("%23s = %7.2f\n", "Hosmer–Lemeshow chi2($df)", χ2)
        Printf.@printf("%23s = %7.4f\n", "Prob > chi2", pv)
    end
    return (; chi2 = χ2, df, pvalue = pv, n, g)
end

"""
    margins_stata(β, V, X; at=nothing, at_labels=nothing,
                  over=nothing, over_levels=nothing,
                  mean_fn=:exp, vce_label="Robust", level=0.95,
                  expression="Predicted number of events, predict()",
                  name="_cons")

Stata-style `margins` with delta-method SE. Three modes:

  - `at = nothing, over = nothing` → **Predictive margins** (sample average of
    `predict` over X). Header: "Predictive margins".

  - `at = c` (length-k vector incl. the constant slot) → **Adjusted predictions**
    at the single point. Pass `at_labels = [:var => v, ...]` to populate the
    "At:" block. Header: "Adjusted predictions".

  - `over = "var" => idx` (factor name and its column index in X) →
    **Predictive margins by factor level**: for each level k, set
    X[:, idx] .= k for ALL observations and compute the sample-average
    margin. Default levels = `sort(unique(X[:, idx]))`; override with
    `over_levels = [...]`. The output is a multi-row table with a sub-header
    for the factor name and one row per level.

For mean_fn=:exp, gradient = (1/N) Σ μ_i x_i (averaged) or μ·c (at-point);
SE = sqrt(g' V g). Pass V_rob (n/(n-1)-corrected) to match Stata's margins
after `poisson, vce(robust)`.
"""
function margins_stata(β::AbstractVector, V::AbstractMatrix, X::AbstractMatrix;
                       at::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector}=nothing,
                       at_labels::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector}=nothing,
                       over::Union{Nothing,Pair}=nothing,
                       over_levels::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector}=nothing,
                       mean_fn::Symbol=:exp, vce_label::String="Robust",
                       level::Float64=0.95, name::String="_cons",
                       expression::String="Predicted number of events, predict()")
    n_sample, _ = size(X)

    g9 = function(x; w_::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w_)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        # Stata's %9.0g effective rule: cap pre-strip at 9 chars EXCEPT for
        # negative |x|<1 where cap=10 (the strip will save 1 char). Without
        # this, negative |x|<1 values lose a digit vs Stata's output.
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w_)
    end
    commafmt(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end
    function _summary_row(margin, se)
        z      = margin / se
        p      = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
        crit   = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
        (margin, se, z, p, margin - crit*se, margin + crit*se)
    end
    function _compute_margin_at_X(Xm)
        if mean_fn == :exp
            μ    = exp.(Xm * β)
            gvec = vec((μ' * Xm) ./ size(Xm, 1))
            margin = Statistics.mean(μ)
        elseif mean_fn == :identity
            μ    = Xm * β
            gvec = vec(Statistics.mean(Xm, dims = 1))
            margin = Statistics.mean(μ)
        elseif mean_fn == :logit
            η    = Xm * β
            μ    = 1 ./ (1 .+ exp.(-η))
            w    = μ .* (1 .- μ)                # ∂Λ/∂η
            gvec = vec((w' * Xm) ./ size(Xm, 1))
            margin = Statistics.mean(μ)
        elseif mean_fn == :probit
            η    = Xm * β
            μ    = Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), η)
            w    = Distributions.pdf.(Distributions.Normal(), η)
            gvec = vec((w' * Xm) ./ size(Xm, 1))
            margin = Statistics.mean(μ)
        else
            error("mean_fn=$mean_fn not supported (use :exp / :identity / :logit / :probit)")
        end
        margin, sqrt(gvec' * V * gvec)
    end

    # Determine title and rows to print
    if over !== nothing
        title = "Predictive margins"
        factor_name, factor_idx = over
        levels_to_use = over_levels === nothing ?
                        sort(unique(X[:, factor_idx])) : collect(over_levels)
        rows = Tuple[]
        for lev in levels_to_use
            Xm = copy(X)
            Xm[:, factor_idx] .= lev
            m, s = _compute_margin_at_X(Xm)
            push!(rows, (lev, _summary_row(m, s)...))
        end
    elseif at === nothing
        title = "Predictive margins"
        m, s  = _compute_margin_at_X(X)
        rows  = [(name, _summary_row(m, s)...)]
    else
        title = "Adjusted predictions"
        c = collect(at)
        length(c) == length(β) ||
            error("at must have length(β)=$(length(β)), got $(length(c))")
        if mean_fn == :exp
            margin = exp(LinearAlgebra.dot(c, β))
            gvec   = margin .* c
        elseif mean_fn == :identity
            margin = LinearAlgebra.dot(c, β)
            gvec   = c
        elseif mean_fn == :logit
            η      = LinearAlgebra.dot(c, β)
            Λ      = 1 / (1 + exp(-η))
            margin = Λ
            gvec   = Λ * (1 - Λ) .* c        # ∂Λ/∂β = Λ(1−Λ)·c
        elseif mean_fn == :probit
            η      = LinearAlgebra.dot(c, β)
            margin = Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
            ϕ      = Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
            gvec   = ϕ .* c                  # ∂Φ/∂β = φ(η)·c
        else
            error("mean_fn=$mean_fn not supported (use :exp / :identity / :logit / :probit)")
        end
        rows = [(name, _summary_row(margin, sqrt(gvec' * V * gvec))...)]
    end

    println()
    Printf.@printf("%-57s%-13s = %5s\n",
                   title, "Number of obs", commafmt(n_sample))
    Printf.@printf("Model VCE: %s\n", vce_label)
    println()
    Printf.@printf("Expression: %s\n", expression)
    if at_labels !== nothing && !isempty(at_labels)
        max_name_w = maximum(length(string(p_.first)) for p_ in at_labels)
        val_strs   = [Printf.@sprintf("%g", float(p_.second)) for p_ in at_labels]
        max_val_w  = maximum(length, val_strs)
        for (i, p_) in enumerate(at_labels)
            prefix = i == 1 ? "At: " : "    "
            Printf.@printf("%s%-*s = %s\n", prefix, max_name_w,
                           string(p_.first), lpad(val_strs[i], max_val_w))
        end
    end
    println()
    println("-"^78)
    println("             |            Delta-method")
    println("             |     Margin   std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95% conf. interval]")
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    if over !== nothing
        Printf.@printf("%12s |\n", first(over))   # factor sub-header row
        for (lev, m, s, z, p, lo, hi) in rows
            lev_str = string(lev isa AbstractFloat && lev == floor(lev) ?
                             Int(lev) : lev)
            Printf.@printf("%11s  | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           lev_str, g9(m; w_=10), g9(s; w_=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p),
                           g9(lo; w_=9), g9(hi; w_=10))
        end
    else
        for (lab, m, s, z, p, lo, hi) in rows
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           lab, g9(m; w_=10), g9(s; w_=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p),
                           g9(lo; w_=9), g9(hi; w_=10))
        end
    end
    println("-"^78)
    return rows
end

"""
    setup_mus10(df10=nothing; vars=nothing, formula=nothing,
                vce=:robust, quiet=true) -> NamedTuple

Universal helper for any chapter that uses the mus10 dataset (`mus10data.dta`,
filtered to `year02 == 1`). Loads the data internally if `df10` is omitted,
drops missings on `vars`, fits Poisson via `poisson_stata`, and returns a
NamedTuple covering everything downstream chunks need — both **Stata-display
order** (`β`, `V`, `X` — slopes first, `_cons` last; for margins / dydx /
lincom / nlcom helpers) and **GLM order** (`model`, `V_robust = fit.V_glm`;
for `test_stata` and other helpers that go through `coefnames(model)`).

Because the helper auto-loads when `df10` is `nothing`, **any chapter chunk
can call `s = setup_mus10()` without first running a chapter-10 data-load
chunk** — i.e. running just chunk 1 + any chapter chunk works.

Defaults:
  - `vars`    = `[:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income, :age]`
                (chapter 10 / 11 set; pass an explicit shorter list for
                chapter-12 Wald tests where `:age` isn't a regressor)
  - `formula` = `docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income`
  - `vce`     = `:robust`
  - `quiet`   = `true` (set `false` to print the regression table)

Examples (indented for clarity):
    s = setup_mus10()                           # load + fit, default 6 vars
    s = setup_mus10(; quiet = false)            # also print the table
    s = setup_mus10(df10)                       # reuse an already-loaded df10
    s = setup_mus10(; vars = [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income])
"""
function setup_mus10(df10=nothing;
                    vars=nothing, formula=nothing,
                    vce::Symbol=:robust, quiet::Bool=true)
    if df10 === nothing
        df10 = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
        # Promote any non-Float64 numeric / LabeledValue columns to plain
        # Float64 so downstream `Float64.(col)` calls don't trip over
        # ReadStatTables' LabeledValue wrapper.
        for c in DataFrames.names(df10)
            col = df10[!, c]
            T   = eltype(col)
            if T <: Union{Missing, Float64}
                continue
            elseif T <: Union{Missing, Float32, Int}
                df10[!, c] = convert.(Union{Missing, Float64}, col)
            else
                # Catch-all: unwrap LabeledValue or any other wrapper via _rawval.
                df10[!, c] = [ismissing(x) ? missing : Float64(_rawval(x))
                              for x in col]
            end
        end
        df10 = DataFrames.filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df10)
    end
    cols = vars === nothing ?
        [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income, :age] : vars
    fml  = formula === nothing ?
        GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income) : formula
    df10c = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:, cols])
    fit = poisson_stata(df10c, fml; vce = vce, quiet = quiet)
    return (; df = df10c, fit,
              model = fit.model, V_robust = fit.V_glm,
              β = fit.β, V = fit.V, X = fit.X,
              n = fit.n, k = fit.k, coefnames = fit.coefnames,
              coefnames_glm = fit.coefnames_glm)
end

"""
    margins_dydx_atmeans_binary_stata(β, V, x_eval, var_idx; link=:logit,
        var_name="x", depvar="y", vce_label="OIM", level=0.95, n_obs=nothing,
        at_labels=nothing, expression=nothing)

Stata-style `margins, dydx(<var>) atmeans` for a binary GLM (logit or
probit). Computes the marginal effect of variable `var_idx` (column
index in `β`, length-k vector) at the point `x_eval` with delta-method
SE.

For the logit link  Λ(η) = 1/(1+e^(-η)):
    ME = β_j · Λ(c'β) · (1 − Λ(c'β))
    ∂ME/∂β_l = δ_{l=j} · Λ(1−Λ)  +  β_j · Λ(1−Λ)(1−2Λ) · c_l

For the probit link  Φ(η):
    ME = β_j · φ(c'β)
    ∂ME/∂β_l = δ_{l=j} · φ(η) − β_j · φ(η) · η · c_l

Prints Stata's `Conditional marginal effects` block (at means form):
header (Number of obs / Model VCE / Expression / dy/dx wrt / At means),
then the single-variable result row (`<var_name> | dy/dx  std. err.  z
P>|z|  [95% CI]`). Returns `(; me, se, z, p, ci_lo, ci_hi)`.
"""
function margins_dydx_atmeans_binary_stata(β::AbstractVector, V::AbstractMatrix,
                                           x_eval::AbstractVector,
                                           var_idx::Int;
                                           link::Symbol = :logit,
                                           var_name::AbstractString = "x",
                                           depvar::AbstractString = "y",
                                           vce_label::AbstractString = "OIM",
                                           level::Float64 = 0.95,
                                           n_obs::Union{Nothing,Int} = nothing,
                                           at_labels::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector} = nothing,
                                           expression::Union{Nothing,AbstractString} = nothing)
    η = LinearAlgebra.dot(x_eval, β)
    if link == :logit
        Λ  = 1 / (1 + exp(-η))
        me = β[var_idx] * Λ * (1 - Λ)
        # Jacobian of ME wrt β
        J  = β[var_idx] .* Λ .* (1 - Λ) .* (1 - 2*Λ) .* x_eval
        J[var_idx] += Λ * (1 - Λ)
    elseif link == :probit
        ϕ  = Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        me = β[var_idx] * ϕ
        J  = -β[var_idx] .* ϕ .* η .* x_eval
        J[var_idx] += ϕ
    else
        error("link=$link not supported (use :logit or :probit)")
    end
    se = sqrt(LinearAlgebra.dot(J, V * J))
    z  = me / se
    p  = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
    crit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = me - crit * se
    ci_hi = me + crit * se

    # Stata `%9.0g` formatter
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    expr = expression === nothing ? "Pr($depvar), predict()" : expression
    println()
    println("Conditional marginal effects" *
            (n_obs === nothing ? "" :
             "                    Number of obs = " * commafmt(n_obs)))
    println("Model VCE: $vce_label")
    println("Expression: $expr")
    println("dy/dx wrt: $var_name")
    if at_labels !== nothing
        for (i, kv) in enumerate(at_labels)
            prefix = i == 1 ? "At  : " : "      "
            Printf.@printf("%s%-12s = %s\n", prefix, string(kv.first),
                           string(kv.second))
        end
    else
        println("At  : (means)")
    end
    println()
    println("-"^78)
    println("             |            Delta-method")
    Printf.@printf("%12s |      dy/dx   std. err.       z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                   "", 100*level)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                   var_name, g9(me; w=10), g9(se; w=9),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p),
                   g9(ci_lo; w=9), g9(ci_hi; w=10))
    println("-"^78)
    return (; me, se, z, p, ci_lo, ci_hi)
end

"""
    margins_dydx_at_binary_stata(β, V, c; specs, link=:logit,
        depvar="y", vce_label="OIM", level=0.95, n_obs=nothing,
        at_labels=nothing, noatlegend=false)

Stata-style `margins, dydx(*) at(...)` (MER) for a binary GLM (logit
or probit). Computes marginal effects at the user-specified point
`c` (length-k vector in β order, with intercept slot included), with
delta-method SEs via the analytic Jacobian.

`specs` is a vector of `(name::String, kind::Symbol, col_idx::Int)`:
- `kind = :continuous` → analytic derivative `ME = β_j · μ'(c'β)`
   - logit:  μ'(η) = Λ(1−Λ),    μ''(η) = Λ(1−Λ)(1−2Λ)
   - probit: μ'(η) = φ(η),      μ''(η) = −η · φ(η)
   Jacobian: e_j · μ'(η) + β_j · μ''(η) · c
- `kind = :factor` → discrete change `ME = μ(c | x_j=1) − μ(c | x_j=0)`
   Jacobian: μ'(η_1)·c_1 − μ'(η_0)·c_0  (where c_1/c_0 set x_j to 1/0)

Output mirrors Stata's `Conditional marginal effects` block for MER
(header / `dy/dx wrt:` / optional `At:` block + the variable rows).
Factor rows print as `1.<name>` per Stata's i.<var> labeling.

Returns `(; rows = Vector{NamedTuple}, c)` where each row has
`(name, me, se, z, p, ci_lo, ci_hi)`.
"""
function margins_dydx_at_binary_stata(β::AbstractVector, V::AbstractMatrix,
                                      c::AbstractVector;
                                      specs::AbstractVector,
                                      link::Symbol = :logit,
                                      depvar::AbstractString = "y",
                                      vce_label::AbstractString = "OIM",
                                      level::Float64 = 0.95,
                                      n_obs::Union{Nothing,Int} = nothing,
                                      at_labels::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector} = nothing,
                                      noatlegend::Bool = false,
                                      expression::Union{Nothing,AbstractString} = nothing)
    # Link evaluators: μ(η), μ'(η), μ''(η)
    if link == :logit
        μfn(η)   = 1 / (1 + exp(-η))
        μ1fn(η)  = (Λ = μfn(η); Λ * (1 - Λ))
        μ2fn(η)  = (Λ = μfn(η); Λ * (1 - Λ) * (1 - 2*Λ))
    elseif link == :probit
        μfn(η)   = Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        μ1fn(η)  = Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        μ2fn(η)  = -η * Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
    else
        error("link=$link not supported (use :logit or :probit)")
    end

    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    rows = NamedTuple[]
    for (name, kind, idx) in specs
        if kind == :continuous
            η  = LinearAlgebra.dot(c, β)
            μ1 = μ1fn(η);  μ2 = μ2fn(η)
            me = β[idx] * μ1
            J  = β[idx] .* μ2 .* c
            J[idx] += μ1
            row_label = name
        elseif kind == :factor
            c1 = copy(c); c1[idx] = 1.0
            c0 = copy(c); c0[idx] = 0.0
            η1 = LinearAlgebra.dot(c1, β); η0 = LinearAlgebra.dot(c0, β)
            me = μfn(η1) - μfn(η0)
            J  = μ1fn(η1) .* c1 .- μ1fn(η0) .* c0
            row_label = "1." * name
        else
            error("kind=$kind not supported (use :continuous or :factor)")
        end
        se = sqrt(LinearAlgebra.dot(J, V * J))
        z  = me / se
        p  = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
        push!(rows, (name = row_label, me = me, se = se, z = z, p = p,
                     ci_lo = me - crit*se, ci_hi = me + crit*se))
    end

    # Stata `%9.0g` formatter
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    expr = expression === nothing ? "Pr($depvar), predict()" : expression
    println()
    # Header: "Conditional marginal effects" left-padded; "Number of obs"
    # right-aligned at col 78. Stata's exact widths: title in 57, label
    # "Number of obs" in 13, " = ", value right-aligned in 5 → total 78.
    if n_obs !== nothing
        Printf.@printf("%-57s%-13s = %5s\n",
                       "Conditional marginal effects",
                       "Number of obs", commafmt(n_obs))
    else
        println("Conditional marginal effects")
    end
    println("Model VCE: $vce_label")
    println()
    println("Expression: $expr")
    println("dy/dx wrt:  ", join([r.name for r in rows], " "))
    if !noatlegend && at_labels !== nothing
        for (i, kv) in enumerate(at_labels)
            prefix = i == 1 ? "At  : " : "      "
            Printf.@printf("%s%-12s = %s\n", prefix, string(kv.first),
                           string(kv.second))
        end
    end
    println()
    # Coefficient table: 12 (name) + 2 ( | ) + 11 (dy/dx) + 11 (se) +
    # 9 (z) + 8 (p) + 13 (ci_lo) + 12 (ci_hi) = 78 chars.
    println("-"^78)
    println("             |            Delta-method")
    Printf.@printf("%12s |      dy/dx   std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                   "", 100*level)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |%s%s%9.2f%8.3f%s%s\n",
                       r.name,
                       g9(r.me;    w=11),
                       g9(r.se;    w=11),
                       r.z, r.p,
                       g9(r.ci_lo; w=13),
                       g9(r.ci_hi; w=12))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    # Stata adds this note when any factor variable appears in the dy/dx list.
    if any(s -> s[2] == :factor, specs)
        println("Note: dy/dx for factor levels is the discrete change from the base level.")
    end
    return (; rows, c)
end

"""
    margins_dydx_ame_binary_stata(β, V, X; specs, link=:logit,
        depvar="y", vce_label="OIM", level=0.95)

Stata-style `margins, dydx(*)` (Average Marginal Effects, AME) for a
binary GLM (logit or probit). Like `margins_dydx_at_binary_stata` but
averaged over the sample rather than evaluated at a single point:

  - Factor j:    ME_j = (1/N) Σ_i [μ(x_iᵀβ | x_j=1) − μ(x_iᵀβ | x_j=0)]
                 J    = (1/N) Σ_i [μ'(η_1i)·c_1i − μ'(η_0i)·c_0i]
  - Continuous:  ME_j = (1/N) Σ_i β_j · μ'(x_iᵀβ)
                 J    = (1/N) Σ_i [e_j · μ'(η_i) + β_j · μ''(η_i) · x_i]

Delta-method SE = √(J' V J). Output mirrors Stata's `Average marginal
effects` block (title, header, table, factor-note footer). Returns
`(; rows)`.
"""
function margins_dydx_ame_binary_stata(β::AbstractVector, V::AbstractMatrix,
                                       X::AbstractMatrix;
                                       specs::AbstractVector,
                                       link::Symbol = :logit,
                                       depvar::AbstractString = "y",
                                       vce_label::AbstractString = "OIM",
                                       level::Float64 = 0.95,
                                       expression::Union{Nothing,AbstractString} = nothing)
    if link == :logit
        μfn(η)   = 1 / (1 + exp(-η))
        μ1fn(η)  = (Λ = μfn(η); Λ * (1 - Λ))
        μ2fn(η)  = (Λ = μfn(η); Λ * (1 - Λ) * (1 - 2*Λ))
        link_label = "logit"
    elseif link == :probit
        μfn(η)   = Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        μ1fn(η)  = Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        μ2fn(η)  = -η * Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        link_label = "probit"
    else
        error("link=$link not supported (use :logit or :probit)")
    end

    n_, k_ = size(X)
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    rows = NamedTuple[]
    for (name, kind, idx) in specs
        if kind == :continuous
            me  = 0.0
            J   = zeros(k_)
            for i in 1:n_
                xi = X[i, :]
                η  = LinearAlgebra.dot(xi, β)
                μ1 = μ1fn(η);  μ2 = μ2fn(η)
                me += β[idx] * μ1
                J  .+= β[idx] .* μ2 .* xi
                J[idx] += μ1
            end
            me /= n_;  J ./= n_
            row_label = name
        elseif kind == :factor
            me = 0.0
            J  = zeros(k_)
            for i in 1:n_
                xi = X[i, :]
                c1 = copy(xi); c1[idx] = 1.0
                c0 = copy(xi); c0[idx] = 0.0
                η1 = LinearAlgebra.dot(c1, β)
                η0 = LinearAlgebra.dot(c0, β)
                me += μfn(η1) - μfn(η0)
                J  .+= μ1fn(η1) .* c1 .- μ1fn(η0) .* c0
            end
            me /= n_;  J ./= n_
            row_label = "1." * name
        else
            error("kind=$kind not supported (use :continuous or :factor)")
        end
        se = sqrt(LinearAlgebra.dot(J, V * J))
        z  = me / se
        p  = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
        push!(rows, (name = row_label, me = me, se = se, z = z, p = p,
                     ci_lo = me - crit*se, ci_hi = me + crit*se))
    end

    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    expr = expression === nothing ? "Pr($depvar), predict()" : expression
    println()
    Printf.@printf("%-57s%-13s = %5s\n",
                   "Average marginal effects",
                   "Number of obs", commafmt(n_))
    println("Model VCE: $vce_label")
    println()
    println("Expression: $expr")
    println("dy/dx wrt:  ", join([r.name for r in rows], " "))
    println()
    println("-"^78)
    println("             |            Delta-method")
    Printf.@printf("%12s |      dy/dx   std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                   "", 100*level)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |%s%s%9.2f%8.3f%s%s\n",
                       r.name,
                       g9(r.me;    w=11),
                       g9(r.se;    w=11),
                       r.z, r.p,
                       g9(r.ci_lo; w=13),
                       g9(r.ci_hi; w=12))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    if any(s -> s[2] == :factor, specs)
        println("Note: dy/dx for factor levels is the discrete change from the base level.")
    end
    return (; rows)
end

"""
    mfx_binary_stata(β, V, X, coefnames; depvar="y", link=:logit,
        at=nothing, level=0.95) -> NamedTuple

Stata's legacy `mfx` (MEM after logit/probit). Auto-detects binary
regressors (column values ⊆ {0, 1}) and uses discrete change for them
(`*` row marker); continuous regressors get the analytic derivative.
Unlike modern `margins, dydx(*)`, both kinds are reported in a single
compact table that includes an `X` column with the at-point value.

Pipeline:
  - Default `at = nothing` ⇒ `c = mean(X, dims=1)` (means)
  - For factor j:    ME = μ(c|x_j=1) − μ(c|x_j=0)
                     J  = μ'(η_1)·c_1 − μ'(η_0)·c_0
  - For continuous:  ME = β_j · μ'(c'β),
                     J  = e_j · μ'(η) + β_j · μ''(η) · c
  - SE = √(J' V J),  z = ME/SE,  Wald p, Normal-based 95% CI.

Output mirrors mfx exactly:

    Marginal effects after <link>
          y  = Pr(<depvar>) (predict)
             =  <Λ̂(c'β)>
    --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    variable |      dy/dx    Std. err.     z    P>|z|  [    95% C.I.   ]      X
    ---------+----------------------------------------------------------------
       <var>*|     ...        ...       ...    ...     ...     ...      ...
    --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    (*) dy/dx is for discrete change of dummy variable from 0 to 1

Returns `(; rows, prob, c)` where each row is `(name, factor, me, se,
z, p, ci_lo, ci_hi, X)`.
"""
function mfx_binary_stata(β::AbstractVector, V::AbstractMatrix,
                          X::AbstractMatrix, coefnames::AbstractVector;
                          depvar::AbstractString = "y",
                          link::Symbol = :logit,
                          at::Union{Nothing, AbstractVector} = nothing,
                          level::Float64 = 0.95)
    c = at === nothing ? vec(Statistics.mean(X, dims = 1)) : collect(at)

    if link == :logit
        μfn(η)  = 1 / (1 + exp(-η))
        μ1fn(η) = (l = μfn(η); l * (1 - l))
        μ2fn(η) = (l = μfn(η); l * (1 - l) * (1 - 2*l))
        link_label = "logit"
    elseif link == :probit
        μfn(η)  = Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        μ1fn(η) = Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        μ2fn(η) = -η * Distributions.pdf(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        link_label = "probit"
    else
        error("link=$link not supported (use :logit or :probit)")
    end

    # Auto-detect binary columns: unique non-missing values ⊆ {0, 1}.
    is_factor = Bool[]
    for (i, name) in enumerate(coefnames)
        if name == "(Intercept)"
            push!(is_factor, false)
            continue
        end
        col = X[:, i]
        u   = unique(col)
        push!(is_factor, length(u) <= 2 && all(v -> v == 0 || v == 1, u))
    end

    η_at = LinearAlgebra.dot(c, β)
    prob = μfn(η_at)
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)

    rows = NamedTuple[]
    for (i, name) in enumerate(coefnames)
        name == "(Intercept)" && continue
        if is_factor[i]
            c1 = copy(c); c1[i] = 1.0
            c0 = copy(c); c0[i] = 0.0
            η1 = LinearAlgebra.dot(c1, β)
            η0 = LinearAlgebra.dot(c0, β)
            me = μfn(η1) - μfn(η0)
            J  = μ1fn(η1) .* c1 .- μ1fn(η0) .* c0
        else
            μ1 = μ1fn(η_at);  μ2 = μ2fn(η_at)
            me = β[i] * μ1
            J  = β[i] .* μ2 .* c
            J[i] += μ1
        end
        se = sqrt(LinearAlgebra.dot(J, V * J))
        z  = me / se
        p  = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z)))
        push!(rows, (name = name, factor = is_factor[i],
                     me = me, se = se, z = z, p = p,
                     ci_lo = me - crit*se, ci_hi = me + crit*se,
                     X = c[i]))
    end

    # Stata-style number formatter (strip leading 0 for |x|<1, no fixed width)
    g(x; sig::Int = 7) = begin
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        s
    end

    println("Marginal effects after $link_label")
    Printf.@printf("      y  = Pr(%s) (predict)\n", depvar)
    Printf.@printf("         =  %s\n", g(prob; sig = 8))
    println("-"^78)
    println("variable |      dy/dx    Std. err.     z    P>|z|  [    95% C.I.   ]      X")
    println("---------+", "-"^68)
    # Column widths chosen to sum to 78 chars including the leading
    # 9-char variable label + "|":
    #   9 (label) + 1 (|) + 11 (dy/dx) + 12 (std err) + 8 (z) + 8 (p)
    #   + 10 (ci_lo) + 9 (ci_hi) + 10 (X) = 78
    for r in rows
        label = lpad(r.factor ? r.name * "*" : r.name * " ", 9)
        Printf.@printf("%s|%s%s%8.2f%8.3f%s%s%s\n",
                       label,
                       lpad(g(r.me;    sig = 7), 11),
                       lpad(g(r.se;    sig = 4), 12),
                       r.z, r.p,
                       lpad(g(r.ci_lo; sig = 5), 10),
                       lpad(g(r.ci_hi; sig = 5),  9),
                       lpad(g(r.X;     sig = 6), 10))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    println("(*) dy/dx is for discrete change of dummy variable from 0 to 1")
    return (; rows, prob, c)
end

"""
    regress_stata(model; level=0.95)

Stata-style `regress` output — prints the ANOVA table, overall F-statistic,
R², adjusted R², Root MSE, and the coefficient table with t-statistics,
p-values, and confidence intervals, matching the format of Stata's
`regress` command. The intercept is relabelled `_cons`.

Works with any `StatsBase`-compatible OLS model, e.g. the output of
`FixedEffectModels.reg(df, @formula(y ~ x2 + x3))`.
"""
function regress_stata(model; level::Float64=0.95, noheader::Bool=false)
    β      = StatsBase.coef(model)
    V      = StatsBase.vcov(model)
    se     = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    nm_raw = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model))
    nm     = replace.(nm_raw, "(Intercept)" => "_cons")
    has_int = any(==("_cons"), nm)

    n      = Int(StatsBase.nobs(model))
    rss    = StatsBase.deviance(model)
    r2     = StatsBase.r2(model)
    ar2    = StatsBase.adjr2(model)
    dof_r  = Int(StatsBase.dof_residual(model))
    k      = length(β) - (has_int ? 1 : 0)
    tss    = rss / max(1 - r2, eps())
    mss    = tss - rss
    rmse   = sqrt(rss / dof_r)
    Fstat  = (mss / k) / (rss / dof_r)
    pF     = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(k, dof_r), Fstat)

    yname = try
        string(StatsBase.responsename(model))
    catch
        hasproperty(model, :yname) ? string(model.yname) : "y"
    end

    t_stat = β ./ se
    tcrit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    p_val  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), abs.(t_stat)))
    ci_lo  = β .- tcrit .* se
    ci_hi  = β .+ tcrit .* se

    # Stata %10.0g-style: `sig` significant digits, strip leading 0 for |x|<1,
    # right-aligned in width `w`.
    function _g(x, w; sig=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, ".")
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, s)
    end

    # ── ANOVA table + summary-stats block (skipped when `noheader=true`,
    # matching Stata's `regress y x, noheader` option)
    if !noheader
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s %10s %10s    %-13s = %10d\n",
                       "Source", "SS", "df", "MS", "Number of obs", n)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^34, "   ",
                Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %10.2f", "F($k, $dof_r)", Fstat))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Model", _g(mss, 10), k, _g(mss/k, 10), "Prob > F", pF)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Residual", _g(rss, 10), dof_r, _g(rss/dof_r, 10),
                       "R-squared", r2)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^34, "   ",
                Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %10.4f", "Adj R-squared", ar2))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Total", _g(tss, 10), n-1, _g(tss/(n-1), 10),
                       "Root MSE", rmse)
    end
    println()

    # ── Coefficient table
    println("-"^78)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s  %9s  %6s  %5s     [%d%% conf. interval]\n",
                   yname, "Coefficient", "Std. err.", "t", "P>|t|",
                   round(Int, 100*level))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for i in eachindex(β)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %6.2f  %5.3f  %s  %s\n",
                       nm[i],
                       _g(β[i], 10),
                       _g(se[i], 9),
                       t_stat[i],
                       p_val[i],
                       _g(ci_lo[i], 11),
                       _g(ci_hi[i], 11))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    return nothing
end

"""
    regress_stata(df, y, xs; level=0.95, vcov=nothing)

Convenience method: fit `y ~ xs…` on `df` with `FixedEffectModels.reg` and
print the Stata-style `regress` output. `y` is the dependent variable (Symbol
or String); `xs` is a Symbol, String, or vector of regressor names. Pass
`vcov=Vcov.robust()` (or similar) for non-default standard errors.

Example:

    regress_stata(df5, :y, [:x2, :x3])
    regress_stata(df5, :y, [:x2, :x3]; vcov=Vcov.robust())
"""
function regress_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, y, xs;
                       level::Float64=0.95, vcov=nothing, weights=nothing,
                       noheader::Bool=false)
    ys  = Symbol(y)
    xsv = xs isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [Symbol(xs)] :
          [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
    f = term(ys) ~ sum(term.(xsv))
    kw = weights === nothing ? (;) : (; weights=Symbol(weights))
    m = vcov === nothing ?
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f; kw...) :
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f, vcov; kw...)
    regress_stata(m; level=level, noheader=noheader)
    return nothing
end

"""
    estat_classification(m, df; depvar="", cutoff=0.5)

Stata-style `estat classification` after a binary model. Prints the
full Stata classification block:

  - Confusion matrix (Classified +/- × True D/~D × Total)
  - "Classified + if predicted Pr(D) >= <cutoff>" / "True D defined as <depvar> != 0"
  - Sensitivity / Specificity / PPV / NPV
  - False+/− rates for true ~D / D / classified +/−
  - Correctly classified

`depvar` is the dependent-variable name shown in the headers (e.g.
`"ins"`). If empty, falls back to the first coefname (best-effort).
"""
function estat_classification(m, df; depvar::AbstractString = "",
                              cutoff::Float64 = 0.5)
    phat = GLM.predict(m, df)
    yhat = Int.(phat .>= cutoff)
    y    = Int.(GLM.response(m))
    tp = sum((yhat .== 1) .& (y .== 1))
    tn = sum((yhat .== 0) .& (y .== 0))
    fp = sum((yhat .== 1) .& (y .== 0))
    fn = sum((yhat .== 0) .& (y .== 1))
    n  = length(y)

    sens = tp / (tp + fn)
    spec = tn / (tn + fp)
    ppv  = tp / (tp + fp)
    npv  = tn / (tn + fn)
    fp_rate_negD = fp / (tn + fp)
    fn_rate_posD = fn / (tp + fn)
    fp_rate_clsP = fp / (tp + fp)
    fn_rate_clsN = fn / (tn + fn)
    correct = (tp + tn) / n

    dv = isempty(depvar) ? string(StatsBase.coefnames(m)[1]) : depvar
    sep_box = "-"^11 * "+" * "-"^26 * "+" * "-"^11
    sep_pct = "-"^50

    println("Logistic model for $dv")
    println()
    println("              -------- True --------")
    println("Classified |         D            ~D  |      Total")
    println(sep_box)
    Printf.@printf("     +     |    %6d        %6d  |    %7d\n",
                   tp, fp, tp + fp)
    Printf.@printf("     -     |    %6d        %6d  |    %7d\n",
                   fn, tn, fn + tn)
    println(sep_box)
    Printf.@printf("   Total   |    %6d        %6d  |    %7d\n",
                   tp + fn, tn + fp, n)
    println()
    Printf.@printf("Classified + if predicted Pr(D) >= %s\n",
                   replace(Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", cutoff),
                           r"^0\." => "."))
    Printf.@printf("True D defined as %s != 0\n", dv)
    println(sep_pct)
    Printf.@printf("%-32sPr( +| D) %7.2f%%\n", "Sensitivity",                 100*sens)
    Printf.@printf("%-32sPr( -|~D) %7.2f%%\n", "Specificity",                 100*spec)
    Printf.@printf("%-32sPr( D| +) %7.2f%%\n", "Positive predictive value",   100*ppv)
    Printf.@printf("%-32sPr(~D| -) %7.2f%%\n", "Negative predictive value",   100*npv)
    println(sep_pct)
    Printf.@printf("%-32sPr( +|~D) %7.2f%%\n", "False + rate for true ~D",        100*fp_rate_negD)
    Printf.@printf("%-32sPr( -| D) %7.2f%%\n", "False - rate for true D",         100*fn_rate_posD)
    Printf.@printf("%-32sPr(~D| +) %7.2f%%\n", "False + rate for classified +",   100*fp_rate_clsP)
    Printf.@printf("%-32sPr( D| -) %7.2f%%\n", "False - rate for classified -",   100*fn_rate_clsN)
    println(sep_pct)
    Printf.@printf("%-42s%7.2f%%\n", "Correctly classified", 100*correct)
    println(sep_pct)

    return (; tp, tn, fp, fn,
              sensitivity = sens, specificity = spec, ppv, npv,
              fp_rate_negD, fn_rate_posD, fp_rate_clsP, fn_rate_clsN,
              accuracy = correct, n)
end

function poisson_stata(df, formula; vce::Symbol=:robust, level::Float64=0.95,
                       quiet::Bool=false,
                       layout::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector}=nothing,
                       header_style::Symbol=:poisson,
                       cluster_var=nothing)
    # Drop missing for variables in formula (and the cluster var, if any)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    cols   = cluster_var === nothing ? needed :
                                       vcat(needed, [Symbol(cluster_var)])
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end

    # Fit Poisson GLM
    m = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    β  = GLM.coef(m)
    cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m))
    yv = Float64.(GLM.response(m))
    μ  = GLM.predict(m)
    Xm = GLM.modelmatrix(m)
    k  = size(Xm, 2)

    # If `cluster_var` is given, force vce → :cluster regardless of caller's
    # choice (Stata's `vce(cluster <var>)` syntax), and capture cluster count.
    n_clusters = 0
    if cluster_var !== nothing
        vce = :cluster
        n_clusters = length(unique(dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]))
    end

    # SE: robust sandwich (default) / cluster-robust (CR1) / OIM.
    # Stata's `vce(robust)` uses n/(n-1) finite-sample correction.
    # `vce(cluster G)` uses (G/(G-1))·(n-1)/(n-k) and aggregates scores by
    # cluster: B = Σ_g (X_g'(y_g − μ_g)) (X_g'(y_g − μ_g))'.
    if vce == :robust
        H = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * Xm
        meat = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal((yv .- μ).^2) * Xm
        Hinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)))
        V = Hinv * meat * Hinv * (n / (n - 1))
    elseif vce == :cluster
        cluster_var === nothing &&
            error("vce = :cluster requires `cluster_var = :varname`")
        cl = dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]
        u  = (yv .- μ) .* Xm                # n×k per-obs scores X_i·(y_i−μ_i)
        # Aggregate scores by cluster, then meat = Σ_g s_g s_g'.
        meat = zeros(k, k)
        for g in unique(cl)
            sg = vec(sum(u[cl .== g, :], dims = 1))
            meat .+= sg * sg'
        end
        H    = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * Xm
        Hinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)))
        G    = n_clusters
        # Stata's `poisson, vce(cluster)` uses ONLY the G/(G−1) cluster
        # adjustment — no extra (n−1)/(n−k) factor (that one is OLS-style).
        V    = Hinv * meat * Hinv * (G / (G - 1))
    else
        V = Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
    end
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z  = β ./ se
    p  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = β .- crit .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ crit .* se

    # Slopes (excluding intercept) — used for both Wald and LR
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:length(β), [intercept_idx])
    Wald = NaN; Wald_p = NaN
    if !isempty(slope_idx)
        β_slope = β[slope_idx]
        V_slope = V[slope_idx, slope_idx]
        Wald = β_slope' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_slope) * β_slope
        Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), Wald)
    end

    # Log pseudolikelihood and Pseudo R² (McFadden's-like: 1 - LL/LL_null)
    ll  = GLM.loglikelihood(m)
    # Null model: intercept only
    m_null = GLM.glm(StatsModels.term(Symbol(formula.lhs)) ~ StatsModels.term(1),
                     dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    ll_null = GLM.loglikelihood(m_null)
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / ll_null

    # LR chi² on slopes — Stata's default `poisson` reports `LR chi2(k)`;
    # `vce(robust|cluster)` switches it to `Wald chi2(k)` (LR is invalid
    # under misspecification of the likelihood).
    LR_chi2 = !isempty(slope_idx) ? 2 * (ll - ll_null) : NaN
    LR_p    = !isempty(slope_idx) ?
              1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), LR_chi2) :
              NaN

    # Stata %9.0g formatter — sign-aware width cap (cap=9 except cap=10 for
    # negative |x|<1, where leading-zero strip saves a char). Without this
    # asymmetry, negative |x|<1 values would lose a digit vs Stata's output.
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(num)
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1
            push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3
        end
        return (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # Skip the entire Stata-style printout when quiet=true (mirrors Stata's
    # `quietly poisson ...`). Useful for chapter chunks that just need β/V/X
    # for downstream margins/dydx/etc. and don't want to repeat the table.
    if !quiet
    # Print Stata-style header. Two layouts:
    #   :poisson — Stata's `poisson` command output. Top-left says "Poisson
    #              regression", and the right column lists Number of obs /
    #              Wald chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 / Pseudo R2 over four lines,
    #              with "Log pseudolikelihood = …" on the last line at left.
    #   :ml      — Stata's `ml maximize` output. No "Poisson regression"
    #              header; the right column lists Number of obs / Wald
    #              chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 over three lines, with "Log
    #              [pseudo]likelihood = …" on the third line at left, and
    #              no Pseudo R2 row.
    println()
    if header_style == :ml
        # Stata `ml maximize` right-block format: 13-char left-padded label,
        # " = ", then a value field whose width is the max of the three
        # value strings plus 1 (so the longest value sits 1 space after `=`,
        # shorter ones are right-aligned). The whole right block is positioned
        # flush right at col 78 by adjusting the leading whitespace.
        nstr = commafmt(n)
        wstr = isfinite(Wald) ? Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", Wald) : ""
        pstr = isfinite(Wald) ? Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", Wald_p) : ""
        vw   = maximum(length, (nstr, wstr, pstr))
        rblock = 13 + 3 + vw
        lead   = max(0, 78 - rblock)
        ws     = " " ^ lead
        println(ws, rpad("Number of obs", 13), " = ", lpad(nstr, vw))
        if isfinite(Wald)
            println(ws, rpad("Wald chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", 13),
                    " = ", lpad(wstr, vw))
        end
        ll_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        ll_str   = Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.3f", ll_label, ll)
        println(rpad(ll_str, lead), rpad("Prob > chi2", 13), " = ", lpad(pstr, vw))
    else
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                       "Poisson regression", "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        # `LR chi2` for OIM (default), `Wald chi2` for robust/cluster.
        chi2_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "Wald" : "LR"
        chi2_val   = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? Wald   : LR_chi2
        chi2_p     = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? Wald_p : LR_p
        if isfinite(chi2_val)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
                           "$chi2_label chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", chi2_val)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", chi2_p)
        end
        ll_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ?
                   "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.5f", ll_label, ll)
        r2_str = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %6.4f", "Pseudo R2", pseudo_r2)
        pad_h  = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(r2_str))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad_h, r2_str)
    end
    println()

    # Cluster sub-note (Stata: "(Std. err. adjusted for G clusters in <var>)"),
    # right-aligned at col 78.
    if vce == :cluster
        cl_str = Printf.@sprintf("(Std. err. adjusted for %d clusters in %s)",
                                 n_clusters, cluster_var)
        println(lpad(cl_str, 78))
    end

    # Coefficient table. Stata uses lowercase "std. err." under the "Robust"
    # subheader for `vce(robust)` / `vce(cluster …)` and capital "Std. err."
    # for the default OIM.
    println("-"^78)
    if vce == :robust || vce == :cluster
        println("             |               Robust")
    end
    se_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "std. err." : "Std. err."
    Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  %s      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
                   string(formula.lhs), se_label)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

    # `_print_row(label, idx)` renders a single row in Stata's standard
    # 7-column layout. `_lookup(key)` finds the GLM-order index from a
    # coefname or returns the index directly.
    _print_row(label, idx) = Printf.@printf(
        "%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
        label, g9(β[idx]; w=10), g9(se[idx]; w=9),
        Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[idx]),
        Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[idx]),
        g9(ci_lo[idx]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[idx]; w=10))
    _lookup(key) = key isa Integer ? Int(key) :
        (let i = findfirst(==(string(key)), cn)
            i === nothing && error("'$(key)' not found in coefnames=$(cn)")
            i
        end)

    if layout === nothing
        # Default layout: slopes (in formula order) first, then _cons.
        for i in slope_idx
            _print_row(cn[i], i)
        end
        intercept_idx !== nothing && _print_row("_cons", intercept_idx)
    else
        # Custom layout. Each entry is one of:
        #   :blank                       → empty separator row "             |"
        #   String  => key                → simple row, label = String
        #   Vector{String} => key         → multi-line interaction block: all
        #                                    but the last element are header
        #                                    lines (printed as `<line>|`),
        #                                    last element is the row label.
        # `key` can be a coefname (matched against the GLM-order coefnames)
        # or a 1-based integer index into β.
        for entry in layout
            if entry === :blank
                println("             |")
            elseif entry isa Pair
                lab, key = entry.first, entry.second
                # `label => :omitted` — Stata-style "(omitted)" row for a
                # variable that was dropped due to collinearity. Prints
                # "        label |          0  (omitted)" with no key lookup.
                if key === :omitted
                    Printf.@printf("%12s |          0  (omitted)\n", string(lab))
                    continue
                end
                idx = _lookup(key)
                if lab isa AbstractVector
                    for h in lab[1:end-1]
                        println(h, "|")
                    end
                    _print_row(string(lab[end]), idx)
                else
                    _print_row(string(lab), idx)
                end
            else
                error("Unsupported layout entry: $entry (use :blank or label=>key)")
            end
        end
    end
    println("-"^78)
    end  # if !quiet

    # Return values in *Stata's display order*: slopes first, then _cons.
    # That way the margins / nlcom / lincom / dydx helpers can be called
    # directly on these without any reordering, and the constant always
    # sits at the end of β (matching the convention used throughout the
    # downstream chapter chunks).
    if intercept_idx === nothing
        ord = collect(slope_idx)
        cn_ord = cn[ord]
    else
        ord = vcat(collect(slope_idx), [intercept_idx])
        cn_ord = vcat(cn[slope_idx], "_cons")
    end
    β_ord  = β[ord]
    se_ord = se[ord]
    V_ord  = V[ord, ord]
    X_ord  = Xm[:, ord]   # last column = ones (the constant)

    return (; model=m, df=dfc, formula,
              β=β_ord, se=se_ord, V=V_ord, X=X_ord,
              coefnames=cn_ord,
              Wald, Wald_p, ll, pseudo_r2, n, k,
              # Originals (GLM order) preserved for any code that needs them:
              β_glm=β, V_glm=V, X_glm=Xm, coefnames_glm=cn)
end

"""
    probit_stata(df, formula; vce=:oim, level=0.95, quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `probit <depvar> <regs> [, vce(robust)]`. Fits a Binomial GLM
with `ProbitLink` and prints Stata's exact `probit` output:

  - Header: Number of obs / LR chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 / Log likelihood / Pseudo R²
    (NB: `LR chi2`, NOT `Wald chi2` — Stata uses 2·(ll − ll_null) for the
    overall fit statistic in `probit` even with `vce(robust)`.)
  - Coefficient table in Stata-display order (slopes first, _cons last).

Returns `(; model, β, se, V, X, coefnames, ll, ll_null, pseudo_r2, n, k,
          β_glm, V_glm, X_glm, coefnames_glm)` so downstream code (e.g.
Heckman two-step) can reuse the fitted probit linear index.
"""
function probit_stata(df, formula; vce::Symbol=:oim, level::Float64=0.95,
                      quiet::Bool=false)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end
    # Drop any rows with non-finite values (NaN/Inf in computed columns
    # like `linc = log(hhincome)` would crash GLM.jl's IRLS at the
    # `isfinite(dev)` assertion). `dropmissing` only handles `Missing`.
    keep = trues(DataFrames.nrow(dfc))
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        eltype(col) <: Real || continue
        for i in eachindex(col)
            keep[i] &= isfinite(col[i])
        end
    end
    dfc = dfc[keep, :]
    # Fit probit. Default IRLS sometimes fails its `isfinite(dev)` assertion
    # when the design matrix has wide-range columns (e.g. `age2`); in that
    # case we warm-start from a logit fit's β rescaled by ≈1/1.81 (the
    # asymptotic logit→probit coefficient ratio sqrt(π/3)).
    m = try
        GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    catch err
        if err isa AssertionError && occursin("isfinite", string(err))
            m_logit = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.LogitLink())
            β_init  = GLM.coef(m_logit) ./ 1.81
            GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink();
                    start = β_init)
        else
            rethrow(err)
        end
    end
    β  = GLM.coef(m); cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m)); k = length(β)
    yv = Float64.(GLM.response(m))
    Xm = GLM.modelmatrix(m)

    V = if vce == :robust
        # Robust sandwich for probit: V = A · meat · A · (n/(n-1)) with
        # A = OIM vcov and meat = Σ s_i s_iᵀ where the per-obs score is
        # s_i = ((y_i − μ_i) / [μ_i(1−μ_i)]) · φ(η_i) · x_i.
        η  = Xm * β                                 # linear index
        μ  = GLM.predict(m)
        ϕ  = Distributions.pdf.(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        u  = (yv .- μ) ./ (μ .* (1 .- μ)) .* ϕ
        s  = u .* Xm
        meat = s' * s
        A = Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))                     # OIM vcov is A⁻¹ already
        A * meat * A * (n / (n - 1))
    else
        Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
    end
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z  = β ./ se
    p_z = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = β .- crit .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ crit .* se

    ll = GLM.loglikelihood(m)
    m_null = GLM.glm(StatsModels.term(Symbol(formula.lhs)) ~ StatsModels.term(1),
                     dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    ll_null = GLM.loglikelihood(m_null)
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / ll_null
    LR = 2 * (ll - ll_null)
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
    LR_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), LR)

    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                       "Probit regression", "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
                       "LR chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", LR)
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", LR_p)
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("Log likelihood = %.4f", ll)
        r2_str = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %6.4f", "Pseudo R2", pseudo_r2)
        pad    = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(r2_str))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad, r2_str)
        println()

        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs), 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                          vcat(slope_idx, [intercept_idx])
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(β[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_z[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
    end

    intercept_idx2 = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx2     = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx2])
    ord2 = intercept_idx2 === nothing ? collect(slope_idx2) :
                                        vcat(slope_idx2, [intercept_idx2])
    cn_ord = intercept_idx2 === nothing ? cn[ord2] :
                                          vcat(cn[slope_idx2], "_cons")
    return (; model = m, β = β[ord2], se = se[ord2], V = V[ord2, ord2],
              X = Xm[:, ord2], coefnames = cn_ord,
              ll, ll_null, pseudo_r2, LR, LR_p, n, k,
```
