```{julia}
              β_glm = β, V_glm = V, X_glm = Xm, coefnames_glm = cn)
end

"""
    ivprobit_stata(df; depvar, exog_vars, endog, instruments,
                   vce=:oim, level=0.95, quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `ivprobit <depvar> <exog_vars> (<endog> = <instruments>)
[, vce(robust)] nolog` — Probit model with one continuous endogenous
regressor, joint MLE.

Model:
    y2_i = 1{x_iᵀβ + γ·y1_i + u_i > 0},          (probit / structural)
    y1_i = z_iᵀπ + δᵀIV_i + v_i,                  (linear / first-stage)
    (u_i, v_i) ∼ N(0, [[1, ρσ_v]; [ρσ_v, σ_v²]])

Estimation: MLE in (β, γ, π, δ, lnσ_v, atanh(ρ)). LBFGS with
ForwardDiff autodiff, warm-started from (probit β; OLS first-stage π,δ;
σ_v from OLS residuals; ρ=0). OIM vcov from finite-difference Hessian
(ForwardDiff through `cdf` is unreliable for Hessians). For
`vce=:robust` we use the sandwich  V = A⁻¹ B A⁻¹ ·n/(n-1)  with
A = -H/n and B = (1/n)Σ s_i s_iᵀ from per-obs scores (computed by
ForwardDiff on the per-obs log-likelihood).

Output mirrors Stata exactly: header (Probit model with endogenous
regressors / Number of obs / Wald chi2 / Log [pseudo]likelihood / Prob
> chi2), structural-equation coefficient table (slopes + linc + _cons),
auxiliary block (`corr(e.linc, e.ins)` and `sd(e.linc)` with their
delta-method CIs from the (atanh ρ, lnσ_v) parameterization), the
Wald test of exogeneity (corr = 0), and the trailing `Endogenous: ...`
/ `Exogenous: ...` lines.

Returns `(; β, γ, π, δ, σ_v, ρ, ll, n, V, coefnames_struct,
coefnames_first, Wald, Wald_p, Wald_exog, Wald_exog_p, model)`.
"""
function ivprobit_stata(df; depvar::Symbol,
                        exog_vars::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                        endog::Symbol,
                        instruments::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                        vce::Symbol = :oim, level::Float64 = 0.95,
                        quiet::Bool = false)
    needed = unique(vcat(depvar, endog, exog_vars, instruments))
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end
    keep = trues(DataFrames.nrow(dfc))
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        eltype(col) <: Real || continue
        for i in eachindex(col)
            keep[i] &= isfinite(col[i])
        end
    end
    dfc = dfc[keep, :]

    y2 = Float64.(dfc[!, depvar])
    y1 = Float64.(dfc[!, endog])
    Xm = hcat(ones(DataFrames.nrow(dfc)),
              [Float64.(dfc[!, v]) for v in exog_vars]...)         # (1, x...)
    Zm = hcat(ones(DataFrames.nrow(dfc)),
              [Float64.(dfc[!, v]) for v in exog_vars]...,
              [Float64.(dfc[!, v]) for v in instruments]...)        # (1, x..., iv...)
    n   = size(Xm, 1)
    k_x = size(Xm, 2)                # _cons + exog_vars
    k_z = size(Zm, 2)                # _cons + exog_vars + instruments
    k_iv = length(instruments)
    cn_struct = vcat([string(v) for v in exog_vars], string(endog), "_cons")
    cn_first  = vcat("_cons", [string(v) for v in exog_vars],
                     [string(v) for v in instruments])

    # ── Initial values ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    # First-stage OLS: y1 ~ Z
    π0_full = Zm \ y1
    v0      = y1 .- Zm * π0_full
    σv0     = max(Statistics.std(v0; corrected = false), 1e-3)
    # Probit warm-start for structural equation: y2 ~ (X, y1)
    Wm = hcat(Xm, y1)                                              # (1, x..., y1)
    m_pr = try
        GLM.glm(Wm, y2, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    catch
        # Fall back to logit warm-start rescaled if probit IRLS diverges
        m_lo = GLM.glm(Wm, y2, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.LogitLink())
        GLM.glm(Wm, y2, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink();
                start = GLM.coef(m_lo) ./ 1.81)
    end
    β_struct0 = GLM.coef(m_pr)                                     # (β_x..., γ)

    # Pack: θ = [β_struct (k_x+1); π_full (k_z); ln σ_v; atanh ρ]
    p_β = k_x + 1
    p_π = k_z
    p_total = p_β + p_π + 2

    function negll(θ)
        β_s   = θ[1:p_β]                            # length k_x + 1: x..., y1
        π_fs  = θ[p_β + 1 : p_β + p_π]              # length k_z (first-stage π)
        ln_σ  = θ[p_β + p_π + 1]
        at_ρ  = θ[p_β + p_π + 2]
        σ_v   = exp(ln_σ)
        ρ_loc = tanh(at_ρ)
        η_y2  = Wm * β_s                            # x_iᵀβ + γ·y1_i
        v     = y1 .- Zm * π_fs
        denom = sqrt(1 - ρ_loc^2 + eps())
        s     = (2 .* y2 .- 1) .* (η_y2 .+ (ρ_loc / σ_v) .* v) ./ denom
        Φs    = Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), s)
        # log(φ(v/σ_v)) - log(σ_v): log normal density of v.
        # NOTE: use `log(2 * pi)` (not `2π`) — `π` is shadowed by `π_fs`
        # in scope-broken named-tuple-ish ways; using the full constant
        # name `pi` is the unambiguous form.
        ll_v = -0.5 .* (v ./ σ_v) .^ 2 .- 0.5 * log(2 * Base.pi) .- ln_σ
        # log of probit term, clamped to avoid -Inf when Φs is tiny.
        ll_y = log.(max.(Φs, 1e-300))
        return -sum(ll_v .+ ll_y)
    end

    θ0 = vcat(β_struct0, π0_full, log(σv0), 0.0)
    res = _optimize_compat(negll, θ0, Optim.LBFGS(),
                         Optim.Options(g_tol = 1e-7, iterations = 2000);
                         autodiff = :forward)
    θ̂  = Optim.minimizer(res)
    ll = -negll(θ̂)

    β_s_hat = θ̂[1:p_β]
    π̂       = θ̂[p_β + 1 : p_β + p_π]
    ln_σv   = θ̂[p_β + p_π + 1]
    at_ρ    = θ̂[p_β + p_π + 2]
    σ_v     = exp(ln_σv)
    ρ       = tanh(at_ρ)

    # ── Hessian / vcov ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    function _fd_hessian(f, x)
        nθ = length(x); H = zeros(nθ, nθ)
        h_ = sqrt(sqrt(eps(Float64))) .* max.(abs.(x), 1.0)
        f0 = f(x)
        for i in 1:nθ
            xpi = copy(x); xmi = copy(x)
            xpi[i] += h_[i]; xmi[i] -= h_[i]
            fpi, fmi = f(xpi), f(xmi)
            H[i, i] = (fpi - 2*f0 + fmi) / h_[i]^2
            for j in (i+1):nθ
                xpp = copy(x); xpp[i] += h_[i]; xpp[j] += h_[j]
                xpm = copy(x); xpm[i] += h_[i]; xpm[j] -= h_[j]
                xmp = copy(x); xmp[i] -= h_[i]; xmp[j] += h_[j]
                xmm = copy(x); xmm[i] -= h_[i]; xmm[j] -= h_[j]
                H[i, j] = H[j, i] =
                    (f(xpp) - f(xpm) - f(xmp) + f(xmm)) / (4 * h_[i] * h_[j])
            end
        end
        return H
    end
    H = _fd_hessian(negll, θ̂)
    A = LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)
    V_oim = LinearAlgebra.inv(A)
    V_full = if vce == :robust
        # Per-obs scores via central finite differences (avoids depending
        # on ForwardDiff being imported in Main; chunk-1 doesn't `using`
        # it directly — Optim only needs it transitively).
        function negll_i(θ, i)
            β_s = θ[1:p_β]; π_fs = θ[p_β+1:p_β+p_π]
            ln_σ = θ[p_β+p_π+1]; at_ρ_loc = θ[p_β+p_π+2]
            σ_v_loc = exp(ln_σ); ρ_loc = tanh(at_ρ_loc)
            η_y2 = LinearAlgebra.dot(Wm[i, :], β_s)
            v_i  = y1[i] - LinearAlgebra.dot(Zm[i, :], π_fs)
            denom = sqrt(1 - ρ_loc^2 + eps())
            s_i  = (2*y2[i] - 1) * (η_y2 + (ρ_loc / σ_v_loc) * v_i) / denom
            Φs   = Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), s_i)
            ll_v = -0.5 * (v_i / σ_v_loc)^2 - 0.5 * log(2 * Base.pi) - ln_σ
            ll_y = log(max(Φs, 1e-300))
            return -(ll_v + ll_y)
        end
        h_g = sqrt(sqrt(eps(Float64))) .* max.(abs.(θ̂), 1.0)
        # Sum of outer products of per-obs scores.
        B = zeros(p_total, p_total)
        sc = zeros(p_total)
        for i in 1:n
            for j in 1:p_total
                xp = copy(θ̂); xp[j] += h_g[j]
                xm = copy(θ̂); xm[j] -= h_g[j]
                sc[j] = (negll_i(xp, i) - negll_i(xm, i)) / (2 * h_g[j])
            end
            B .+= sc * sc'
        end
        # Sandwich: V_oim · B · V_oim, multiplied by n/(n-1) correction
        V_oim * B * V_oim * (n / (n - 1))
    else
        V_oim
    end

    se_full = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_full), 0.0))
    se_β    = se_full[1:p_β]
    se_lnσ  = se_full[p_β + p_π + 1]
    se_atρ  = se_full[p_β + p_π + 2]

    # Reorder structural β to Stata-display order:
    # exog_vars... in formula order, then endog (linc), then _cons.
    # Currently β_s_hat = (_cons, exog_vars..., endog).
    n_x = length(exog_vars)
    ord_b = vcat(2:n_x+1, [n_x + 2], [1])
    β_disp  = β_s_hat[ord_b]
    se_disp = se_β[ord_b]
    V_disp  = V_full[1:p_β, 1:p_β][ord_b, ord_b]

    # Wald chi² on slopes (excludes _cons, INCLUDES endog).
    slope_idx_disp = 1:length(ord_b)-1   # everything except last (_cons)
    Wald = β_disp[slope_idx_disp]' *
           LinearAlgebra.inv(V_disp[slope_idx_disp, slope_idx_disp]) *
           β_disp[slope_idx_disp]
    Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx_disp)), Wald)

    # Wald test of exogeneity (corr = 0): test atanh(ρ) = 0.
    Wald_exog   = (at_ρ / se_atρ)^2
    Wald_exog_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(1), Wald_exog)

    # Delta-method SEs and CIs for σ_v and ρ (transform CI ends back).
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    z_disp = β_disp ./ se_disp
    p_disp = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_disp)))
    ci_lo  = β_disp .- crit .* se_disp
    ci_hi  = β_disp .+ crit .* se_disp

    σv_lo = exp(ln_σv - crit * se_lnσ)
    σv_hi = exp(ln_σv + crit * se_lnσ)
    ρ_lo  = tanh(at_ρ - crit * se_atρ)
    ρ_hi  = tanh(at_ρ + crit * se_atρ)
    se_σv = σ_v * se_lnσ                   # delta-method on exp
    se_ρ  = (1 - ρ^2) * se_atρ             # delta-method on tanh

    # ── Print ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        nstr = commafmt(n)
        wstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", Wald)
        pstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", Wald_p)
        vw = maximum(length, (nstr, wstr, pstr))
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %*s\n",
                       "Probit model with endogenous regressors",
                       "Number of obs", vw, nstr)
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %*s\n", "",
                       "Wald chi2($(length(slope_idx_disp)))", vw, wstr)
        ll_label = vce == :robust ? "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.4f", ll_label, ll)
        right  = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %*s", "Prob > chi2", vw, pstr)
        pad_h  = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(right))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad_h, right)
        println()

        println("-"^78)
        if vce == :robust
            println("             |               Robust")
        end
        se_label = vce == :robust ? "std. err." : "Std. err."
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  %s      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(depvar), se_label, 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        # Body: exog_vars..., endog, _cons
        for (i, lab) in enumerate(vcat([string(v) for v in exog_vars],
                                       string(endog), "_cons"))
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           lab, g9(β_disp[i]; w=10), g9(se_disp[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_disp[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_disp[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        # Auxiliary block: corr(e.linc, e.ins), sd(e.linc)
        Printf.@printf("%12s |\n", " corr(e.$endog,")
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s%26s%s  %s\n",
                       "       e.$depvar)",
                       g9(ρ; w=10), g9(se_ρ; w=9), "",
                       g9(ρ_lo; w=9), g9(ρ_hi; w=10))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s%26s%s  %s\n",
                       "  sd(e.$endog)",
                       g9(σ_v; w=10), g9(se_σv; w=9), "",
                       g9(σv_lo; w=9), g9(σv_hi; w=10))
        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("Wald test of exogeneity (corr = 0): chi2(1) = %.2f%8sProb > chi2 = %.4f\n",
                       Wald_exog, "", Wald_exog_p)
        println("Endogenous: ", string(endog))
        exo_full = vcat([string(v) for v in exog_vars],
                        [string(v) for v in instruments])
        # Wrap at ~12 chars after "Exogenous: " to mimic Stata's line wrap.
        prefix = "Exogenous:  "
        line   = prefix
        for w in exo_full
            if length(line) + length(w) + 1 > 78
                println(line)
                line = "            " * w
            else
                line *= (line == prefix ? "" : " ") * w
            end
        end
        println(line)
    end

    return (; β = β_disp, se = se_disp, V = V_disp,
              γ = β_disp[length(exog_vars) + 1],
              π = π̂, σ_v, ρ, ln_σv, at_ρ,
              se_σv, se_ρ, σv_lo, σv_hi, ρ_lo, ρ_hi,
              ll, n, Wald, Wald_p, Wald_exog, Wald_exog_p,
              coefnames_struct = cn_struct,
              coefnames_first  = cn_first,
              model = m_pr, V_full)
end

"""
    ivprobit_twostep_stata(df; depvar, exog_vars, endog, instruments,
                           level=0.95, quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `ivprobit <depvar> <exog_vars> (<endog> = <instruments>),
twostep first` — Newey (1987) two-step / control-function IV probit.

Pipeline:
  1. **First stage**: OLS of `<endog>` on `[exog_vars; instruments]`
     (with intercept). Reports the standard `regress` table including
     SS / df / MS / F / R²; printed by `regress_stata`.
  2. Compute first-stage residual  v̂_i = y1_i − z_iᵀπ̂.
  3. **Second stage**: probit of `<depvar>` on `[exog_vars; <endog>; v̂]`.
     The probit coefficients on `[exog_vars; <endog>]` are the two-step
     IV-probit estimates of the structural equation.
  4. Wald test of exogeneity: `(z-stat on v̂)² ~ χ²(1)`.

The reported second-stage SEs are the augmented-probit OIM SEs (i.e.
treating v̂ as a regressor) rather than Newey's exact two-step
correction. Point estimates and the Wald exogeneity statistic match
Stata's `twostep` exactly; the SEs and CIs are an approximation that
ignores first-stage variability.

Output mirrors Stata's two-block layout (first-stage table + second-
stage block with `Wald test of exogeneity` and Endogenous/Exogenous
variable lists). Returns
`(; first_stage, β_struct, se_struct, V_struct, γ, V_aug, λ̂, se_λ,
Wald_exog, Wald_exog_p, n, model_second)`.
"""
function ivprobit_twostep_stata(df; depvar::Symbol,
                                exog_vars::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                                endog::Symbol,
                                instruments::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                                level::Float64 = 0.95,
                                quiet::Bool = false)
    needed = unique(vcat(depvar, endog, exog_vars, instruments))
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end
    keep = trues(DataFrames.nrow(dfc))
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        eltype(col) <: Real || continue
        for i in eachindex(col)
            keep[i] &= isfinite(col[i])
        end
    end
    dfc = dfc[keep, :]

    # ── First stage: OLS y1 on (exog + IV) ────────────────────────────
    fs_rhs   = vcat(exog_vars, instruments)
    fs_form  = StatsModels.term(endog) ~ sum(StatsModels.term.(fs_rhs))
    m_first  = FixedEffectModels.reg(dfc, fs_form)
    quiet || regress_stata(m_first; level = level)
    yhat     = FixedEffectModels.predict(m_first, dfc)
    dfc.vhat_ivp = Float64.(dfc[!, endog]) .- yhat

    # ── Second stage: probit y2 on (exog + endog + vhat) ─────────────
    ss_rhs   = vcat(exog_vars, endog, :vhat_ivp)
    ss_form  = StatsModels.term(depvar) ~ sum(StatsModels.term.(ss_rhs))
    m_aug    = probit_stata(dfc, ss_form; quiet = true)
    cn_aug   = m_aug.coefnames_glm                          # GLM order
    β_aug    = m_aug.β_glm
    V_aug    = m_aug.V_glm
    n_obs    = m_aug.n

    # Indices for structural equation (everything except v̂):
    idx_v    = findfirst(==("vhat_ivp"), cn_aug)
    idx_int  = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn_aug)
    idx_keep = setdiff(1:length(β_aug), [idx_v])      # struct: x..., endog, _cons
    # Stata-display order: exog_vars in formula order, then endog, then _cons.
    order_struct = Int[]
    for v in exog_vars
        push!(order_struct, findfirst(==(string(v)), cn_aug))
    end
    push!(order_struct, findfirst(==(string(endog)), cn_aug))
    push!(order_struct, idx_int)

    β_struct  = β_aug[order_struct]
    V_struct  = V_aug[order_struct, order_struct]
    se_struct = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_struct), 0.0))

    # Wald test of exogeneity = (z on vhat)²
    se_λ = sqrt(max(V_aug[idx_v, idx_v], 0.0))
    λ̂   = β_aug[idx_v]
    Wald_exog   = (λ̂ / se_λ)^2
    Wald_exog_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(1), Wald_exog)

    # Wald chi² on slopes for header (excludes _cons, includes endog).
    slope_idx = 1:length(order_struct) - 1
    Wald_struct = β_struct[slope_idx]' *
                  LinearAlgebra.inv(V_struct[slope_idx, slope_idx]) *
                  β_struct[slope_idx]
    Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)),
                                   Wald_struct)

    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    z_struct  = β_struct ./ se_struct
    p_struct  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_struct)))
    ci_lo     = β_struct .- crit .* se_struct
    ci_hi     = β_struct .+ crit .* se_struct

    # ── Print second-stage block ──────────────────────────────────────
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        nstr = commafmt(n_obs)
        wstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", Wald_struct)
        pstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", Wald_p)
        vw = maximum(length, (nstr, wstr, pstr))
        Printf.@printf("%-50s%-15s = %*s\n",
                       "Two-step probit with endogenous regressors",
                       "Number of obs", vw, nstr)
        Printf.@printf("%50s%-15s = %*s\n", "",
                       "Wald chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", vw, wstr)
        Printf.@printf("%50s%-15s = %*s\n", "", "Prob > chi2", vw, pstr)
        println()

        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       "", 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        labels = vcat([string(v) for v in exog_vars], string(endog), "_cons")
        for i in eachindex(order_struct)
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           labels[i], g9(β_struct[i]; w=10), g9(se_struct[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_struct[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_struct[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("Wald test of exogeneity: chi2(1) = %.2f%19sProb > chi2 = %.4f\n",
                       Wald_exog, "", Wald_exog_p)
        println("Endogenous: ", string(endog))
        exo_full = vcat([string(v) for v in exog_vars],
                        [string(v) for v in instruments])
        prefix = "Exogenous:  "
        line   = prefix
        for w in exo_full
            if length(line) + length(w) + 1 > 78
                println(line)
                line = "            " * w
            else
                line *= (line == prefix ? "" : " ") * w
            end
        end
        println(line)
    end

    return (; first_stage = m_first,
              β_struct, se_struct, V_struct,
              γ = β_struct[length(exog_vars) + 1],
              V_aug, λ̂, se_λ,
              Wald_exog, Wald_exog_p,
              Wald = Wald_struct, Wald_p,
              n = n_obs, model_second = m_aug.model)
end

"""
    ivregress_2sls_stata(df; depvar, exog_vars, endog, instruments,
                         vce=:default, level=0.95, noheader=false, quiet=false)
        -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `ivregress 2sls <depvar> <exog_vars> (<endog> = <instruments>)
[, vce(robust)] [noheader]`. Two-stage least squares via
`FixedEffectModels.reg` with the standard `(endog ~ instruments)`
syntax.

Output mirrors Stata's `ivregress 2sls` block:
  - Optional header (Instrumental variables 2SLS regression / Number
    of obs / F / Prob > F / R² / Adj R² / Root MSE) — skipped when
    `noheader=true`
  - Coefficient table (with "Robust" sub-banner under `vce=:robust`)
  - Trailing `Endogenous: <endog>` / `Exogenous: <exog + IV>` footer

Returns `(; model, β, se, V, coefnames, n)`. Pass `vce=:robust` for
heteroskedasticity-robust SEs (matches Stata's `vce(robust)`).
"""
function ivregress_2sls_stata(df; depvar::Symbol,
                              exog_vars::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                              endog::Symbol,
                              instruments::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                              vce::Symbol = :default,
                              level::Float64 = 0.95,
                              noheader::Bool = false,
                              quiet::Bool = false)
    needed = unique(vcat(depvar, endog, exog_vars, instruments))
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end
    keep = trues(DataFrames.nrow(dfc))
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        eltype(col) <: Real || continue
        for i in eachindex(col)
            keep[i] &= isfinite(col[i])
        end
    end
    dfc = dfc[keep, :]

    # Build FixedEffectModels formula with (endog ~ instruments) IV block
    fml_iv = StatsModels.term(depvar) ~
             sum(StatsModels.term.(exog_vars)) +
             (StatsModels.term(endog) ~ sum(StatsModels.term.(instruments)))
    m = vce == :robust ?
        FixedEffectModels.reg(dfc, fml_iv, FixedEffectModels.Vcov.robust()) :
        FixedEffectModels.reg(dfc, fml_iv)

    β  = FixedEffectModels.coef(m)
    V  = FixedEffectModels.vcov(m)
    cn = String.(StatsBase.coefnames(m))
    n  = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m))
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z  = β ./ se
    p  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = β .- crit .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ crit .* se

    # Stata-display order: exog_vars in formula order, endog, then _cons.
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    order = Int[]
    for v in exog_vars
        push!(order, findfirst(==(string(v)), cn))
    end
    push!(order, findfirst(==(string(endog)), cn))
    intercept_idx !== nothing && push!(order, intercept_idx)
    labels = vcat([string(v) for v in exog_vars], string(endog),
                  intercept_idx === nothing ? String[] : ["_cons"])

    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # Wald chi² on slopes (excludes _cons), R², Root MSE — used by header.
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:length(β), [intercept_idx])
    Wald, Wald_p, R2_val, RMSE = NaN, NaN, NaN, NaN
    if !isempty(slope_idx)
        β_s = β[slope_idx]; V_s = V[slope_idx, slope_idx]
        Wald   = β_s' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_s) * β_s
        Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), Wald)
    end
    try
        R2_val = StatsBase.r2(m)
    catch
    end
    try
        rss   = sum((Float64.(dfc[!, depvar]) .-
                     FixedEffectModels.predict(m, dfc)) .^ 2)
        dof_r = max(n - length(β), 1)
        RMSE  = sqrt(rss / dof_r)
    catch
    end

    if !quiet
        if !noheader
            # Stata header layout: title in 50 chars; right block uses
            # "<label padded to 16> = <value right-aligned in 10>" → 78.
            Printf.@printf("%-50s%-16s= %10s\n",
                           "Instrumental-variables 2SLS regression",
                           "Number of obs", g9(Float64(n); w=10))
            isfinite(Wald) && Printf.@printf("%50s%-16s= %10s\n", "",
                "Wald chi2($(length(slope_idx)))",
                Printf.@sprintf("%10.2f", Wald))
            isfinite(Wald_p) && Printf.@printf("%50s%-16s= %10s\n", "",
                "Prob > chi2", Printf.@sprintf("%10.4f", Wald_p))
            isfinite(R2_val) && Printf.@printf("%50s%-16s= %10s\n", "",
                "R-squared", Printf.@sprintf("%10.4f", R2_val))
            isfinite(RMSE) && Printf.@printf("%50s%-16s= %10s\n", "",
                "Root MSE", g9(RMSE; w=10))
            println()
        end
        println("-"^78)
        if vce == :robust
            println("             |               Robust")
        end
        se_label = vce == :robust ? "std. err." : "Std. err."
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  %s      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(depvar), se_label, 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        for (i, idx) in enumerate(order)
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           labels[i], g9(β[idx]; w=10), g9(se[idx]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[idx]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[idx]),
                           g9(ci_lo[idx]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[idx]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
        println("Endogenous: ", string(endog))
        exo_full = vcat([string(v) for v in exog_vars],
                        [string(v) for v in instruments])
        prefix = "Exogenous:  "
        line   = prefix
        for w in exo_full
            if length(line) + length(w) + 1 > 78
                println(line)
                line = "            " * w
            else
                line *= (line == prefix ? "" : " ") * w
            end
        end
        println(line)
    end

    return (; model = m, β = β[order], se = se[order], V = V[order, order],
              coefnames = labels, n)
end

"""
    estat_overid_2sls_stata(df; depvar, exog_vars, endog, instruments,
                            quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata's `estat overid` after `ivregress 2sls`. Computes the Sargan /
Hansen score test of overidentifying restrictions:

  - Re-fit 2SLS, get residuals `û`.
  - Auxiliary OLS  `û ~ exog + instruments`  (full instrument set).
  - Statistic = n · R²  ~  χ²(L − K),  with L = # excluded instruments
    and K = # endogenous regressors.

Prints Stata's standard block:

      Test of overidentifying restrictions:

      Score chi2(L−K)          =  <stat>  (p = <p>)

Returns `(; chi2, df, pvalue)`.
"""
function estat_overid_2sls_stata(df; depvar::Symbol,
                                 exog_vars::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                                 endog::Symbol,
                                 instruments::AbstractVector{Symbol},
                                 quiet::Bool = false)
    fit = ivregress_2sls_stata(df;
        depvar = depvar, exog_vars = exog_vars,
        endog = endog, instruments = instruments,
        quiet = true)
    m = fit.model
    yhat = FixedEffectModels.predict(m, df)
    yvec = Float64.(df[!, depvar])
    keep = .!ismissing.(yhat) .& isfinite.(yvec) .& isfinite.(yhat)
    uhat = yvec[keep] .- yhat[keep]

    # Auxiliary regression of û on (exog + instruments + intercept).
    n_aux = length(uhat)
    Z = hcat(ones(n_aux),
             [Float64.(df[keep, v]) for v in exog_vars]...,
             [Float64.(df[keep, v]) for v in instruments]...)
    γ̂  = Z \ uhat
    res_aux = uhat .- Z * γ̂
    ss_tot  = sum(uhat .^ 2)                 # uncentered (no demean — matches Sargan)
    R2  = 1 - sum(res_aux .^ 2) / ss_tot
    chi2  = n_aux * R2
    df_st = length(instruments) - 1   # L_excl − K_endog (single endogenous regressor)
    pv    = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(df_st), chi2)

    if !quiet
        # Strip leading 0 for |x|<1 in Stata's display style
        g(x) = (s = Printf.@sprintf("%.6g", x);
                0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s)
        println()
        println("  Test of overidentifying restrictions:")
        println()
        Printf.@printf("  Score chi2(%d)          =  %s  (p = %.4f)\n",
                       df_st, g(chi2), pv)
    end
    return (; chi2, df = df_st, pvalue = pv)
end

"""
    logit_stata(df, formula; vce=:oim, level=0.95, quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `logit <depvar> <regs> [, vce(robust)]`. Fits a Binomial GLM
with `LogitLink` and prints Stata's exact `logit` output:

  - Header: "Logistic regression" + Number of obs / LR chi2(k) / Prob > chi2
    / Log likelihood / Pseudo R²
  - Coefficient table in Stata-display order (slopes first, _cons last).

Returns `(; model, β, se, V, X, coefnames, ll, ll_null, pseudo_r2, n, k,
LR, LR_p, β_glm, V_glm, X_glm, coefnames_glm)`. Mirrors `probit_stata`
field-for-field so downstream margins/dydx/lincom helpers can swap
between the two without changes.
"""
function logit_stata(df, formula; vce::Symbol=:oim, level::Float64=0.95,
                     quiet::Bool=false, cluster_var=nothing)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    cols   = cluster_var === nothing ? needed :
                                       vcat(needed, [Symbol(cluster_var)])
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end
    m  = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.LogitLink())
    β  = GLM.coef(m); cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m)); k = length(β)
    yv = Float64.(GLM.response(m))
    Xm = GLM.modelmatrix(m)

    V = if vce == :robust
        # Robust sandwich: meat = Σ s_i s_iᵀ with score s_i = (y_i − μ_i)·x_i
        μ    = GLM.predict(m)
        s    = (yv .- μ) .* Xm
        meat = s' * s
        A    = Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
        A * meat * A * (n / (n - 1))
    elseif vce == :cluster
        cluster_var === nothing &&
            error("vce = :cluster requires `cluster_var = :varname`")
        cl = dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]
        μ  = GLM.predict(m)
        u  = (yv .- μ) .* Xm                # n×k per-obs scores
        meat = zeros(k, k)
        for g in unique(cl)
            sg = vec(sum(u[cl .== g, :], dims = 1))
            meat .+= sg * sg'
        end
        A = Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
        G = length(unique(cl))
        # Stata's `logit, vce(cluster)` uses ONLY the G/(G−1) cluster
        # adjustment (no extra (n−1)/(n−k) factor).
        A * meat * A * (G / (G - 1))
    else
        Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
    end
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z  = β ./ se
    p_z = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = β .- crit .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ crit .* se

    ll = GLM.loglikelihood(m)
    m_null = GLM.glm(StatsModels.term(Symbol(formula.lhs)) ~ StatsModels.term(1),
                     dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.LogitLink())
    ll_null = GLM.loglikelihood(m_null)
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / ll_null
    LR = 2 * (ll - ll_null)
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
    LR_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), LR)

    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # For robust / cluster vce, Stata switches to Wald chi² (computed on
    # the slopes using the robust V) and Log pseudolikelihood.
    is_rob = vce == :robust || vce == :cluster
    Wald, Wald_p = NaN, NaN
    if is_rob && !isempty(slope_idx)
        β_s = β[slope_idx]
        V_s = V[slope_idx, slope_idx]
        Wald   = β_s' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_s) * β_s
        Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), Wald)
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                       "Logistic regression", "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        if is_rob
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
                           "Wald chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", Wald)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", Wald_p)
        else
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
                           "LR chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", LR)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", LR_p)
        end
        ll_label = is_rob ? "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.4f", ll_label, ll)
        r2_str = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %6.4f", "Pseudo R2", pseudo_r2)
        pad    = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(r2_str))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad, r2_str)
        println()

        # Cluster sub-note (Stata: "(Std. err. adjusted for G clusters in <var>)").
        if vce == :cluster
            G = length(unique(dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]))
            cl_str = Printf.@sprintf("(Std. err. adjusted for %d clusters in %s)",
                                     G, cluster_var)
            println(lpad(cl_str, 78))
        end

        println("-"^78)
        if is_rob
            println("             |               Robust")
        end
        se_label = is_rob ? "std. err." : "Std. err."
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  %s      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs), se_label, 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                          vcat(slope_idx, [intercept_idx])
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(β[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_z[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
    end

    intercept_idx2 = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx2     = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx2])
    ord2 = intercept_idx2 === nothing ? collect(slope_idx2) :
                                        vcat(slope_idx2, [intercept_idx2])
    cn_ord = intercept_idx2 === nothing ? cn[ord2] :
                                          vcat(cn[slope_idx2], "_cons")
    return (; model = m, β = β[ord2], se = se[ord2], V = V[ord2, ord2],
              X = Xm[:, ord2], coefnames = cn_ord,
              ll, ll_null, pseudo_r2, LR, LR_p, n, k,
              β_glm = β, V_glm = V, X_glm = Xm, coefnames_glm = cn)
end

"""
    hetprob_stata(df, formula_mean, het_vars; level=0.95, quiet=false)
        -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `hetprob <depvar> <indeps>, het(<het_vars>) nolog`.
Heteroskedastic probit:

    y_i = 1{x_iᵀβ + ε_i > 0},   ε_i ~ N(0, σ_i²),   σ_i = exp(z_iᵀγ)

The variance specification carries no constant (absorbed into β's
scale), so `γ` has length `length(het_vars)`. Estimation by MLE
(LBFGS with ForwardDiff autodiff), warm-started from a plain probit.
OIM vcov from the analytic Hessian of the negative log-likelihood.

Output mirrors Stata: header (Number of obs / Zero / Nonzero outcomes
/ Wald chi2(k_β-slopes) / Log likelihood / Prob > chi2), a two-block
coefficient table (`<depvar>` block + `lnsigma` block), and the
`LR test of lnsigma=0: chi2(q)` line.

`het_vars` is a `Vector{Symbol}` (or anything convertible). Returns
`(; β, γ, se_β, se_γ, V, ll, ll_probit, LR, LR_p, Wald, Wald_p, n,
n_zero, n_one, k_x, k_z, coefnames_x, coefnames_z, X, Z, model)`.
"""
function hetprob_stata(df, formula_mean, het_vars; level::Float64 = 0.95,
                       quiet::Bool = false)
    het_syms = Symbol.(het_vars)
    needed   = unique(vcat(StatsModels.termvars(formula_mean), het_syms))
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end

    # Build X (mean equation, with intercept) and Z (variance equation, no
    # intercept — Stata's hetprob convention).
    m_pr = GLM.glm(formula_mean, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    β0   = GLM.coef(m_pr); cn_x = GLM.coefnames(m_pr)
    Xm   = GLM.modelmatrix(m_pr)
    yv   = Float64.(GLM.response(m_pr))
    Z    = hcat([Float64.(dfc[!, v]) for v in het_syms]...)
    cn_z = String.(het_syms)
    n    = size(Xm, 1)
    k_x  = size(Xm, 2)
    k_z  = size(Z, 2)

    # Negative log-likelihood (jointly in (β, γ))
    function negll(θ)
        β = θ[1:k_x]; γ = θ[k_x+1:end]
        σ = exp.(Z * γ)
        s = (2 .* yv .- 1.0) .* (Xm * β) ./ σ
        return -sum(log.(max.(Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), s),
                              1e-300)))
    end
    θ0  = vcat(β0, zeros(k_z))
    res = _optimize_compat(negll, θ0, Optim.LBFGS(),
                         Optim.Options(g_tol = 1e-9, iterations = 1000);
                         autodiff = :forward)
    θ̂   = Optim.minimizer(res)
    β̂   = θ̂[1:k_x]
    γ̂   = θ̂[k_x+1:end]
    ll  = -negll(θ̂)
    ll_probit = GLM.loglikelihood(m_pr)
    LR  = 2 * (ll - ll_probit)
    LR_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(k_z), LR)

    # OIM vcov via finite-difference Hessian (avoids ForwardDiff through
    # CDF a second time).
    function _fd_hessian(f, x)
        n_p = length(x); H = zeros(n_p, n_p)
        h   = sqrt(sqrt(eps(Float64))) .* max.(abs.(x), 1.0)
        f0  = f(x)
        for i in 1:n_p, j in i:n_p
            xpp = copy(x); xpp[i] += h[i]; xpp[j] += h[j]
            xmm = copy(x); xmm[i] -= h[i]; xmm[j] -= h[j]
            if i == j
                xp = copy(x); xp[i] += h[i]
                xm = copy(x); xm[i] -= h[i]
                H[i, i] = (f(xp) - 2*f0 + f(xm)) / h[i]^2
            else
                xpm = copy(x); xpm[i] += h[i]; xpm[j] -= h[j]
                xmp = copy(x); xmp[i] -= h[i]; xmp[j] += h[j]
                H[i, j] = H[j, i] =
                    (f(xpp) - f(xpm) - f(xmp) + f(xmm)) / (4 * h[i] * h[j])
            end
        end
        return H
    end
    H = _fd_hessian(negll, θ̂)
    V = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H))
    se_full = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    se_β = se_full[1:k_x]
    se_γ = se_full[k_x+1:end]
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)

    # Wald chi² on β slopes (excluding intercept)
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn_x)
    slope_x = setdiff(1:k_x, [intercept_idx])
    Wald, Wald_p = NaN, NaN
    if !isempty(slope_x)
        β_s   = β̂[slope_x]
        V_s   = V[slope_x, slope_x]
        Wald  = β_s' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_s) * β_s
        Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_x)), Wald)
    end

    # Stata `%9.0g` formatter
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(num)
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    n_one  = sum(yv .== 1)
    n_zero = n - n_one

    # Print Stata-format output
    if !quiet
        println()
        # Header (right column auto-sized; ~8 chars wide for the values)
        nstr = commafmt(n)
        z0   = commafmt(n_zero)
        z1   = commafmt(n_one)
        wstr = isfinite(Wald) ? Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", Wald) : ""
        pstr = isfinite(Wald) ? Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", Wald_p) : ""
        vw   = maximum(length, (nstr, z0, z1, wstr, pstr))
        Printf.@printf("%-48s%-18s= %*s\n",
                       "Heteroskedastic probit model", "Number of obs", vw, nstr)
        Printf.@printf("%48s%-18s= %*s\n", "", "Zero outcomes", vw, z0)
        Printf.@printf("%48s%-18s= %*s\n", "", "Nonzero outcomes", vw, z1)
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%48s%-18s= %*s\n", "",
                       "Wald chi2($(length(slope_x)))", vw, wstr)
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("Log likelihood = %.3f", ll)
        right  = Printf.@sprintf("%-18s= %*s", "Prob > chi2", vw, pstr)
        pad_h  = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(right))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad_h, right)
        println()

        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula_mean.lhs), 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        # ins (mean) block — equation header, then slopes, then _cons
        println(rpad(string(formula_mean.lhs), 12), " |")
        z_β   = β̂ ./ se_β
        p_β   = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_β)))
        ci_lo_β = β̂ .- crit .* se_β
        ci_hi_β = β̂ .+ crit .* se_β
        ord_x = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_x) :
                                            vcat(slope_x, [intercept_idx])
        for i in ord_x
            label = cn_x[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn_x[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(β̂[i]; w=10), g9(se_β[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_β[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_β[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo_β[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi_β[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        # lnsigma block
        println(rpad("lnsigma", 12), " |")
        z_γ   = γ̂ ./ se_γ
        p_γ   = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_γ)))
        ci_lo_γ = γ̂ .- crit .* se_γ
        ci_hi_γ = γ̂ .+ crit .* se_γ
        for i in 1:k_z
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           cn_z[i], g9(γ̂[i]; w=10), g9(se_γ[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_γ[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_γ[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo_γ[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi_γ[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)

        # LR test footer
        Printf.@printf("LR test of lnsigma=0: chi2(%d) = %.2f%26sProb > chi2 = %.4f\n",
                       k_z, LR, "", LR_p)
    end

    return (; β = β̂, γ = γ̂, se_β, se_γ, V, ll, ll_probit, LR, LR_p,
              Wald, Wald_p, n, n_zero, n_one, k_x, k_z,
              coefnames_x = cn_x, coefnames_z = cn_z,
              X = Xm, Z, model = m_pr)
end

"""
    ols_specs_stata(df, formula; robust=false) -> NamedTuple

Fit `regress y x1 x2 …[, vce(robust)]` via GLM (Gaussian / Identity) and
return the NamedTuple that `estimates_table_stata` consumes:
`(; β, se, coefnames, n, ll)` in slopes-first / _cons-last order. Robust
SEs use HC1: `V_HC1 = (n/(n-k))·(X'X)⁻¹ X'diag(ê²)X (X'X)⁻¹`. The OLS
log-likelihood matches Stata's `e(ll)`.
"""
function ols_specs_stata(df, formula; robust::Bool = false)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end
    m  = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Normal(), GLM.IdentityLink())
    β  = GLM.coef(m); cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m)); k = length(β)
    ll = GLM.loglikelihood(m)
    se = if robust
        Xm = GLM.modelmatrix(m)
        y  = Float64.(GLM.response(m))
        e  = y .- Xm * β
        Hinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(Xm' * Xm))
        V    = Hinv * (Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(e .^ 2) * Xm) * Hinv *
               (n / (n - k))
        sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V))
    else
        sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(GLM.vcov(m)))
    end
    # Slopes first, _cons last
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx     = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
    ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                      vcat(collect(slope_idx), [intercept_idx])
    cn_ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? cn[ord] :
                                          vcat(cn[slope_idx], "_cons")
    return (; β = β[ord], se = se[ord], coefnames = cn_ord, n, ll)
end

"""
    estimates_table_stata(specs::AbstractVector;
                          stats=[:N, :ll], max_per_block=5)

Stata-style `estimates table m1 m2 …, t stats(N ll) b(%7.3f) stfmt(%8.2f)`.
Compares multiple fitted models side-by-side, with point estimates on
the first line of each variable's row and the t-statistic (β/SE) on the
second.

Each `spec` is a NamedTuple with:
- `name::String`        — column label (e.g. "blogit")
- `eq::String`          — equation block label. Models with the same
                          `eq` share a block; OLS conventionally uses
                          `"_"` to separate it from logit/probit which
                          live under the depvar (e.g. `"ins"`).
- `β::Vector{<:Real}`   — point estimates in `coefnames` order
- `se::Vector{<:Real}`  — standard errors
- `coefnames::Vector{String}`  — variable names (`_cons` or
                          `(Intercept)` accepted for the constant)
- `n::Int`              — number of observations
- `ll::Real`            — log-likelihood (also defined for OLS via the
                          Gaussian likelihood, matching Stata's `e(ll)`)

Splits into chunks of `max_per_block` model columns. Within each chunk
the union of all `(eq, var)` pairs across **all** specs is shown — so a
chunk with only OLS still shows the empty `ins` block, exactly as Stata
displays it. Returns `nothing`; output is text.
"""
function estimates_table_stata(specs::AbstractVector;
                               stats::AbstractVector{Symbol} = [:N, :ll],
                               max_per_block::Int = 5)
    var_w = 12
    col_w = 11
    nice(v) = v == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : v

    # Collect all (eq, var) pairs across ALL specs in order of first
    # appearance. That way a chunk containing only OLS still shows the
    # empty `ins` block above.
    eqvars = Tuple{String,String}[]
    for s in specs, v in s.coefnames
        tup = (s.eq, nice(v))
        tup in eqvars || push!(eqvars, tup)
    end
    eqs = String[]
    for (eq, _) in eqvars
        eq in eqs || push!(eqs, eq)
    end

    fmt_b(x)  = Printf.@sprintf("%11.3f", x)
    fmt_t(x)  = Printf.@sprintf("%11.2f", x)
    fmt_n(x)  = Printf.@sprintf("%11d",   x)
    fmt_ll(x) = Printf.@sprintf("%11.2f", x)
    blank     = " "^col_w

    n_blocks = ceil(Int, length(specs) / max_per_block)
    for b in 1:n_blocks
        ix    = ((b-1)*max_per_block + 1):min(b*max_per_block, length(specs))
        chunk = specs[ix]
        nc    = length(chunk)
        line_w = var_w + 2 + nc * col_w
        println("-" ^ line_w)

        # Header row: "    Variable | <name1> <name2> ..."
        print(lpad("Variable", var_w), " |")
        for c in chunk
            print(lpad(c.name, col_w))
        end
        println()
        println("-" ^ var_w, "+", "-" ^ (line_w - var_w - 1))

        # Per-equation blocks
        for eq in eqs
            println(rpad(eq, var_w), " |")
            vars_in_eq = [v for (e, v) in eqvars if e == eq]
            for v in vars_in_eq
                # Coefficient row
                print(lpad(v, var_w), " |")
                for c in chunk
                    if c.eq == eq
                        cnames = nice.(c.coefnames)
                        i      = findfirst(==(v), cnames)
                        print(i === nothing ? blank : fmt_b(c.β[i]))
                    else
                        print(blank)
                    end
                end
                println()
                # t-statistic row
                print(" " ^ var_w, " |")
                for c in chunk
                    if c.eq == eq
                        cnames = nice.(c.coefnames)
                        i      = findfirst(==(v), cnames)
                        print(i === nothing ? blank :
                              fmt_t(c.β[i] / c.se[i]))
                    else
                        print(blank)
                    end
                end
                println()
            end
            println("-" ^ var_w, "+", "-" ^ (line_w - var_w - 1))
        end

        # Statistics block
        println(rpad("Statistics", var_w), " |")
        for st in stats
            print(lpad(string(st), var_w), " |")
            for c in chunk
                if st == :N
                    print(fmt_n(c.n))
                elseif st == :ll
                    print(fmt_ll(c.ll))
                else
                    val = getfield(c, st)
                    print(Printf.@sprintf("%11g", val))
                end
            end
            println()
        end
        println("-" ^ line_w)
        println(lpad("Legend: b/t", line_w))
        println()
    end
    return nothing
end

"""
    nbreg_stata(df, formula; vce=:oim, level=0.95, quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `nbreg <depvar> <regs>, [vce(robust)] nolog`. Fits the NB2
model jointly in (β, lnα) by maximising the log-likelihood

    lnf_i = lnΓ(y_i + 1/α) − lnΓ(1/α) − lnΓ(y_i + 1)
            − (y_i + 1/α) · ln(1 + α·μ_i) + y_i·ln(α) + y_i·θ_i,
    θ_i = x_iᵀβ,  μ_i = exp(θ_i)

via `Optim.LBFGS` with autodiff and uses the inverse Hessian as the OIM
vcov. Prints the Stata header (Number of obs / LR chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 /
Pseudo R²) followed by the coefficient table with `/lnalpha` and `alpha`
rows, and finally the LR test of `α = 0` (NB → Poisson) reported as
`chibar2(01)` with the half-mixture p-value `0.5·P(χ²₁ > LR)`.

Returns `(; model, β_glm, V_glm, coefnames_glm, lnα, α, ll, n, k,
LR_alpha, p_chibar)`.
"""
function nbreg_stata(df, formula; vce::Symbol=:oim, level::Float64=0.95,
                    quiet::Bool=false, cluster_var=nothing)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    cols   = cluster_var === nothing ? needed :
                                       vcat(needed, [Symbol(cluster_var)])
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end

    # Fit Poisson first: gives β starting values + LL_pois for the LR test
    m_pois  = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    β0      = GLM.coef(m_pois)
    ll_pois = GLM.loglikelihood(m_pois)
    yv      = Float64.(GLM.response(m_pois))
    Xm      = GLM.modelmatrix(m_pois)
    cn      = GLM.coefnames(m_pois)
    n       = size(Xm, 1)
    k       = size(Xm, 2)

    # NB log-likelihood (parameters are β stacked with lnα — last entry)
    function nb_nll(p)
        β  = p[1:k]; α = exp(p[k + 1])
        η  = Xm * β; μ = exp.(η); inv_α = 1 / α
        ll = sum(SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(yv .+ inv_α) .-
                 SpecialFunctions.loggamma(inv_α) .-
                 SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(yv .+ 1) .-
                 (yv .+ inv_α) .* log.(1 .+ α .* μ) .+
                 yv .* log(α) .+ yv .* η)
        return -ll
    end
    # Use NelderMead (derivative-free) to avoid forwarding ForwardDiff Duals
    # through `SpecialFunctions.gamma_inc`, which lacks Dual methods and
    # produces "no method matching" errors during autodiff. We get a high-
    # quality optimum from LBFGS (warm-started from Poisson β) but refine via
    # NelderMead and use central finite differences for the Hessian.
    p0  = Float64.(vcat(β0, log(1.0)))
    res = _optimize_compat(nb_nll, p0, Optim.NelderMead(),
                         Optim.Options(g_tol     = 1e-10,
                                       x_abstol  = 1e-10,
                                       f_reltol  = 1e-12,
                                       iterations = 5000))
    p̂   = Float64.(Optim.minimizer(res))
    β̂   = p̂[1:k]
    lnα = p̂[k + 1]
    α   = exp(lnα)
    ll  = -nb_nll(p̂)::Float64

    # OIM vcov from inverse Hessian via central finite differences (avoids
    # any autodiff path through gamma_inc / loggamma).
    function _fd_hessian(f::Function, x::AbstractVector{<:Real})
        n_p = length(x)
        H   = zeros(n_p, n_p)
        h   = sqrt(sqrt(eps(Float64))) .* max.(abs.(x), 1.0)  # ~1e-4 step
        f0  = f(x)
        for i in 1:n_p
            xpi = copy(x); xmi = copy(x)
            xpi[i] += h[i]; xmi[i] -= h[i]
            fpi, fmi = f(xpi), f(xmi)
            H[i, i] = (fpi - 2*f0 + fmi) / h[i]^2
            for j in (i+1):n_p
                xpp = copy(x); xpp[i] += h[i]; xpp[j] += h[j]
                xpm = copy(x); xpm[i] += h[i]; xpm[j] -= h[j]
                xmp = copy(x); xmp[i] -= h[i]; xmp[j] += h[j]
                xmm = copy(x); xmm[i] -= h[i]; xmm[j] -= h[j]
                H[i, j] = H[j, i] =
                    (f(xpp) - f(xpm) - f(xmp) + f(xmm)) / (4 * h[i] * h[j])
            end
        end
        return H
    end
    H = _fd_hessian(nb_nll, p̂)
    V_oim = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H))
    # For `vce = :robust` / `:cluster`, build the sandwich vcov:
    #   V = A⁻¹ B A⁻¹ · correction
    # with A = OIM Hessian. B is the meat:
    #   robust : B = Σ_i s_i s_iᵀ                      (correction = n/(n-1))
    #   cluster: B = Σ_g (Σ_{i∈g} s_i)(Σ_{i∈g} s_i)ᵀ   (correction = G/(G-1))
    # Per-obs scores via central finite differences (gamma_inc-safe).
    V = if vce == :robust || vce == :cluster
        function nb_nll_i(p, i)
            β_l = p[1:k]; α_l = exp(p[k + 1])
            η_i  = LinearAlgebra.dot(view(Xm, i, :), β_l)
            μ_i  = exp(η_i); inv_α = 1 / α_l
            ll_i = SpecialFunctions.loggamma(yv[i] + inv_α) -
                   SpecialFunctions.loggamma(inv_α) -
                   SpecialFunctions.loggamma(yv[i] + 1) -
                   (yv[i] + inv_α) * log(1 + α_l * μ_i) +
                   yv[i] * log(α_l) + yv[i] * η_i
            return -ll_i
        end
        h_g  = sqrt(sqrt(eps(Float64))) .* max.(abs.(p̂), 1.0)
        # Per-obs score matrix S (n × (k+1)).
        S = zeros(n, k + 1)
        for i in 1:n, j in 1:(k + 1)
            xp = copy(p̂); xp[j] += h_g[j]
            xm = copy(p̂); xm[j] -= h_g[j]
            S[i, j] = (nb_nll_i(xp, i) - nb_nll_i(xm, i)) / (2 * h_g[j])
        end
        if vce == :robust
            B = S' * S
            V_oim * B * V_oim * (n / (n - 1))
        else
            cluster_var === nothing &&
                error("vce = :cluster requires `cluster_var = :varname`")
            cl = dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]
            B  = zeros(k + 1, k + 1)
            for g in unique(cl)
                sg = vec(sum(S[cl .== g, :], dims = 1))
                B .+= sg * sg'
            end
            G = length(unique(cl))
            V_oim * B * V_oim * (G / (G - 1))
        end
    else
        V_oim
    end
    se_full = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    se_β    = se_full[1:k]
    se_lnα  = se_full[k + 1]
    se_α    = α * se_lnα                   # delta method on exp(lnα)

    # CIs
    crit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    z_β   = β̂ ./ se_β
    p_β   = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_β)))
    ci_lo_β = β̂ .- crit .* se_β
    ci_hi_β = β̂ .+ crit .* se_β
    lnα_lo, lnα_hi = lnα - crit*se_lnα, lnα + crit*se_lnα
    α_lo,   α_hi   = exp(lnα_lo),       exp(lnα_hi)

    # Null model (intercept-only NB) for pseudo R². Closed form for β:
    # β̂_0 = log(mean(y)). For α we do a 1D maximization (Nelder–Mead, no
    # autodiff — autodiff into `loggamma`/`gamma_inc` doesn't always have
    # ForwardDiff methods, so we keep the null fit derivative-free).
    ȳ      = Statistics.mean(yv)
    β0_null = log(ȳ)
    function nb_ll_null_α(α::Float64)
        μ = fill(ȳ, length(yv))
        inv_α = 1 / α
        sum(SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(yv .+ inv_α) .-
            SpecialFunctions.loggamma(inv_α) .-
            SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(yv .+ 1) .-
            (yv .+ inv_α) .* log.(1 .+ α .* μ) .+
            yv .* log(α) .+ yv .* β0_null)
    end
    res0 = _optimize_compat(α -> -nb_ll_null_α(exp(α[1])), [log(1.0)],
                          Optim.NelderMead())
    α̂_null   = exp(Float64(Optim.minimizer(res0)[1]))
    ll_null  = nb_ll_null_α(α̂_null)
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / ll_null

    # LR chi2 (model vs intercept only) — NB likelihood ratio
    LR    = 2 * (ll - ll_null)
    LR_p  = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(k - 1), LR)

    # LR for α = 0 (NB vs Poisson). Half-mixture p-value: 0.5 · P(χ²₁ > LR)
    LR_α  = 2 * (ll - ll_pois)
    p_chibar = LR_α <= 0 ? 1.0 :
               0.5 * Distributions.ccdf(Distributions.Chisq(1), LR_α)

    # Stata `%9.0g` formatter (sign-aware, see `poisson_stata`)
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(num)
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # Wald chi² on slopes (used in robust header instead of LR).
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx     = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
    Wald, Wald_p = NaN, NaN
    if !isempty(slope_idx)
        β_s = β̂[slope_idx]; V_s = V[slope_idx, slope_idx]
        Wald   = β_s' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_s) * β_s
        Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)),
                                       Wald)
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        # Header (`poisson`-style: title left, right column auto-sized)
        is_rob = vce == :robust || vce == :cluster
        nstr = commafmt(n)
        chi2_label = is_rob ? "Wald" : "LR"
        chi2_val   = is_rob ? Wald   : LR
        chi2_p     = is_rob ? Wald_p : LR_p
        wstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", chi2_val)
        pstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", chi2_p)
        rstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", pseudo_r2)
        vw   = maximum(length, (nstr, wstr, pstr, rstr))
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %*s\n",
                       "Negative binomial regression", "Number of obs", vw, nstr)
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %*s\n", "",
                       "$chi2_label chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", vw, wstr)
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %*s\n",
                       "Dispersion: mean", "Prob > chi2", vw, pstr)
        ll_label = is_rob ? "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %*s\n",
                       Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.4f", ll_label, ll),
                       "Pseudo R2", vw, rstr)
        println()

        # Cluster sub-note (Stata: "(Std. err. adjusted for G clusters in <var>)").
        if vce == :cluster
            G = length(unique(dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]))
            cl_str = Printf.@sprintf("(Std. err. adjusted for %s clusters in %s)",
                                     commafmt(G), cluster_var)
            println(lpad(cl_str, 78))
        end

        # Coefficient table — Stata order: slopes first, _cons last, then
        # /lnalpha and alpha.
        ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                          vcat(slope_idx, [intercept_idx])
        println("-"^78)
        if is_rob
            println("             |               Robust")
        end
        se_label = is_rob ? "std. err." : "Std. err."
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  %s      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs), se_label, 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(β̂[i]; w=10), g9(se_β[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_β[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_β[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo_β[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi_β[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s%26s%s  %s\n",
                       "/lnalpha", g9(lnα; w=10), g9(se_lnα; w=9), "",
                       g9(lnα_lo; w=9), g9(lnα_hi; w=10))
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s%26s%s  %s\n",
                       "alpha", g9(α; w=10), g9(se_α; w=9), "",
                       g9(α_lo; w=9), g9(α_hi; w=10))
        println("-"^78)
        # LR α=0 footer — only printed for OIM (Stata omits it under
        # `vce(robust)` because the LR test isn't valid under
        # misspecified likelihood).
        if !is_rob
            chibar_str = LR_α >= 1e4 ? Printf.@sprintf("%.1e", LR_α) :
                         Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", LR_α)
            Printf.@printf("LR test of alpha=0: chibar2(01) = %-15s Prob >= chibar2 = %.3f\n",
                           chibar_str, p_chibar)
        end
    end

    return (; model = m_pois, β_glm = β̂, V_glm = V[1:k, 1:k],
              coefnames_glm = cn,
              lnα, se_lnα, α, se_α,
              ll, ll_pois, ll_null, pseudo_r2,
              n, k, LR, LR_p, LR_α, p_chibar)
end
```

## 14.4 Example

### 14.4.1 Data description

```{julia}
#=
clear
* Load data
use musr/mus14data.dta
* Interaction variables
drop age2 agefem agechr agewhi
* Summary statistics of variables
global xlist age hstatusg hhincome educyear married hisp
generate linc = ln(hhinc)
global extralist linc female white chronic adl sretire
summarize ins retire $xlist $extralist
=#
#=
clear
* Load data
use musr/mus14data.dta
* Interaction variables
drop age2 agefem agechr agewhi
* Summary statistics of variables
global xlist age hstatusg hhincome educyear married hisp
generate linc = ln(hhinc)
global extralist linc female white chronic adl sretire
summarize ins retire $xlist $extralist
=#

# Load mus14data, drop the four interaction columns Stata recreates later,
# add linc = log(hhincome), and run `summarize_stata` (chunk 1) on the
# combined `xlist + extralist` variable list.
df14 = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus14data.dta"))
for c in DataFrames.names(df14)
    if eltype(df14[!, c]) <: Union{Missing, Float32}
        df14[!, c] = convert.(Union{Missing, Float64}, df14[!, c])
    end
end
DataFrames.select!(df14, DataFrames.Not([:age2, :agefem, :agechr, :agewhi]))
# Stata's `gen linc = log(hhincome)` returns missing for hhincome ≤ 0.
# Mimic that here so GLM.jl's IRLS doesn't get fed non-finite values.
df14.linc = [(ismissing(h) || h <= 0) ? missing : log(Float64(h))
             for h in df14.hhincome]

xlist      = [:age, :hstatusg, :hhincome, :educyear, :married, :hisp]
extralist  = [:linc, :female, :white, :chronic, :adl, :sretire]
summarize_stata(df14, vcat([:ins, :retire], xlist, extralist));
```

### 14.4.2 logit regression

```{julia}
#=
* Logit regression
logit ins retire $xlist
=#
#=
* Logit regression
logit ins retire $xlist
=#

# `logit_stata` (chunk 1) fits a Binomial GLM with LogitLink and prints
# Stata's exact `logit` table: "Logistic regression" header with Number
# of obs / LR chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 / Log likelihood / Pseudo R², and
# the coefficient table in slopes-first / _cons-last order.
logit_fit = logit_stata(df14,
    GLM.@formula(ins ~ retire + age + hstatusg + hhincome + educyear +
                       married + hisp));
```

### 14.4.3 Comparison of binary models and parameter estimates

```{julia}
#=
* Estimation of several models
quietly logit ins retire $xlist
estimates store blogit
quietly probit ins retire $xlist 
estimates store bprobit
quietly regress ins retire $xlist 
estimates store bols
quietly logit ins retire $xlist, vce(robust)
estimates store blogitr
quietly probit ins retire $xlist, vce(robust)
estimates store bprobitr
quietly regress ins retire $xlist, vce(robust)
estimates store bolsr
=#
#=
* Estimation of several models
quietly logit ins retire $xlist
estimates store blogit
quietly probit ins retire $xlist
estimates store bprobit
quietly regress ins retire $xlist
estimates store bols
quietly logit ins retire $xlist, vce(robust)
estimates store blogitr
quietly probit ins retire $xlist, vce(robust)
estimates store bprobitr
quietly regress ins retire $xlist, vce(robust)
estimates store bolsr

* Table for comparing models
estimates table blogit blogitr bprobit bprobitr bols bolsr, /*
   */ t stats(N ll) b(%7.3f) stfmt(%8.2f)
=#

# Fit the six models via the chunk-1 helpers (logit_stata / probit_stata /
# ols_specs_stata), then `estimates_table_stata` (chunk 1) renders the
# Stata `estimates table … , t stats(N ll)` side-by-side comparison with
# point estimates on the b-row and t = β/SE on the t-row. Logit/probit
# coefficients appear under the depvar equation block ("ins"), regress
# under "_" (Stata's convention for OLS without an equation prefix).
fml_ins = GLM.@formula(ins ~ retire + age + hstatusg + hhincome +
                              educyear + married + hisp)

blogit   = logit_stata(df14,  fml_ins;                  quiet = true)
blogitr  = logit_stata(df14,  fml_ins; vce = :robust,   quiet = true)
bprobit  = probit_stata(df14, fml_ins;                  quiet = true)
bprobitr = probit_stata(df14, fml_ins; vce = :robust,   quiet = true)
bols     = ols_specs_stata(df14, fml_ins; robust = false)
bolsr    = ols_specs_stata(df14, fml_ins; robust = true)

specs = [
    (name = "blogit",   eq = "ins", β = blogit.β,   se = blogit.se,
                                    coefnames = blogit.coefnames,
                                    n = blogit.n,   ll = blogit.ll),
    (name = "blogitr",  eq = "ins", β = blogitr.β,  se = blogitr.se,
                                    coefnames = blogitr.coefnames,
                                    n = blogitr.n,  ll = blogitr.ll),
    (name = "bprobit",  eq = "ins", β = bprobit.β,  se = bprobit.se,
                                    coefnames = bprobit.coefnames,
                                    n = bprobit.n,  ll = bprobit.ll),
    (name = "bprobitr", eq = "ins", β = bprobitr.β, se = bprobitr.se,
                                    coefnames = bprobitr.coefnames,
                                    n = bprobitr.n, ll = bprobitr.ll),
    (name = "bols",     eq = "_",   β = bols.β,     se = bols.se,
                                    coefnames = bols.coefnames,
                                    n = bols.n,     ll = bols.ll),
    (name = "bolsr",    eq = "_",   β = bolsr.β,    se = bolsr.se,
                                    coefnames = bolsr.coefnames,
                                    n = bolsr.n,    ll = bolsr.ll),
]
estimates_table_stata(specs);
```

## 14.5 Hypothesis and specification tests

### 14.5.1 Wald tests

```{julia}
#=
* Wald test for zero interactions
generate age2 = age*age
generate agefem = age*female
generate agechr = age*chronic
generate agewhi = age*white
global intlist age2 agefem agechr agewhi
quietly logit ins retire $xlist $intlist
test $intlist 
=#
#=
* Wald test for zero interactions
generate age2 = age*age
generate agefem = age*female
generate agechr = age*chronic
generate agewhi = age*white
global intlist age2 agefem agechr agewhi
quietly logit ins retire $xlist $intlist
test $intlist
=#

# Add the four interaction columns to df14 (idempotent — overwrites any
# existing values), fit logit quietly via the chunk-1 helper, and run
# the joint Wald test of `H0: age2 = agefem = agechr = agewhi = 0`
# using `test_stata` (chunk 1).
df14.age2    = df14.age .* df14.age
df14.agefem  = df14.age .* df14.female
df14.agechr  = df14.age .* df14.chronic
df14.agewhi  = df14.age .* df14.white

fml_int = GLM.@formula(ins ~ retire + age + hstatusg + hhincome + educyear +
                              married + hisp +
                              age2 + agefem + agechr + agewhi)
logit_int_fit = logit_stata(df14, fml_int; quiet = true)

test_stata(logit_int_fit.model, ["age2", "agefem", "agechr", "agewhi"];
           depvar = "ins");
```

### 14.5.2 likelihood-ratio tests

```{julia}
#=
* Likelihood-ratio test
quietly logit ins retire $xlist $intlist
estimates store B 
quietly logit ins retire $xlist
lrtest B
=#
#=
* Likelihood-ratio test
quietly logit ins retire $xlist $intlist
estimates store B
quietly logit ins retire $xlist
lrtest B
=#

# Fit the unrestricted (with the four interactions) and restricted (xlist
# only) logits quietly via the chunk-1 helper, then `lrtest_stata`
# (chunk 1) computes  LR = 2·(ll_unr − ll_res)  ~  χ²(df)  and prints
# Stata's standard `lrtest` block. df = 4 (restrictions).
fml_unr = GLM.@formula(ins ~ retire + age + hstatusg + hhincome + educyear +
                              married + hisp +
                              age2 + agefem + agechr + agewhi)
fml_res = GLM.@formula(ins ~ retire + age + hstatusg + hhincome + educyear +
                              married + hisp)

logit_unr = logit_stata(df14, fml_unr; quiet = true)
logit_res = logit_stata(df14, fml_res; quiet = true)

lrtest_stata(logit_unr.ll, logit_res.ll, 4);
```

### 14.5.3 Additional model-specification tests

#### Lagrange multiplier test of generalized logit

```{julia}
#=
* Heteroskedastic probit model
hetprob ins retire $xlist, het(chronic) nolog // Heteroskedastic Probit 
=#
#=
* Heteroskedastic probit model
hetprob ins retire $xlist, het(chronic) nolog // Heteroskedastic Probit
=#

# `hetprob_stata` (chunk 1) fits the heteroskedastic probit
#     y = 1{x'β + ε > 0},  ε ~ N(0, σ²),  σ = exp(z'γ)
# jointly in (β, γ) by MLE (LBFGS, ForwardDiff autodiff, warm-started
# from a plain probit), with OIM SEs from the Hessian. Prints Stata's
# exact `hetprob` output: header (Number of obs / Zero / Nonzero
# outcomes / Wald chi2 / Log likelihood / Prob > chi2), the two-block
# coefficient table (`ins` + `lnsigma`), and the LR test of σ-constancy.
hetprob_stata(df14,
    GLM.@formula(ins ~ retire + age + hstatusg + hhincome + educyear +
                        married + hisp),
    [:chronic]);
```

```{julia}
#=
* Stukel score or LM test for asymmetric h-family logit
quietly logit ins retire $xlist
predict xbhat, xb
generate xbhatsq = xbhat^2
quietly logit ins retire $xlist xbhatsq
test xbhatsq
=#
#=
* Stukel score or LM test for asymmetric h-family logit
quietly logit ins retire $xlist
predict xbhat, xb
generate xbhatsq = xbhat^2
quietly logit ins retire $xlist xbhatsq
test xbhatsq
=#

# Stukel's LM/score test for the asymmetric h-family logit. Fit the base
# logit, build xbhat (linear index) and xbhatsq, refit with the squared
# index added, and test H0: γ_{xbhatsq} = 0 via `test_stata` (chunk 1) —
# under H0 this is the LM/Wald form of Stukel's test.
fml_base = GLM.@formula(ins ~ retire + age + hstatusg + hhincome +
                              educyear + married + hisp)
base_fit = logit_stata(df14, fml_base; quiet = true)

df14.xbhat   = base_fit.X_glm * base_fit.β_glm
df14.xbhatsq = df14.xbhat .^ 2

fml_stukel = GLM.@formula(ins ~ retire + age + hstatusg + hhincome +
                                 educyear + married + hisp + xbhatsq)
stukel_fit = logit_stata(df14, fml_stukel; quiet = true)

test_stata(stukel_fit.model, "xbhatsq"; depvar = "ins");
```

#### Heteroskedastic probit regression

```{julia}
#=
* Heteroskedastic probit model
hetprob ins retire $xlist, het(chronic) nolog // Heteroskedastic Probit
=#
#=
* Heteroskedastic probit model
hetprob ins retire $xlist, het(chronic) nolog // Heteroskedastic Probit
=#

# Same `hetprob` command as the LM-test sub-section above; reproduced
# here under the "Heteroskedastic probit regression" heading. The
# `hetprob_stata` (chunk 1) helper handles the full Stata layout.
hetprob_stata(df14,
    GLM.@formula(ins ~ retire + age + hstatusg + hhincome + educyear +
                        married + hisp),
    [:chronic]);
```

### 14.6.4 The predict command for fitted probabilities

```{julia}
#=
* Calculate and summarize fitted probabilities
quietly logit ins hhincome
predict plogit, pr
quietly probit ins hhincome  
predict pprobit, pr
quietly regress ins hhincome
predict pols, xb
summarize ins plogit pprobit pols
=#
#=
* Calculate and summarize fitted probabilities
quietly logit ins hhincome
predict plogit, pr
quietly probit ins hhincome
predict pprobit, pr
quietly regress ins hhincome
predict pols, xb
summarize ins plogit pprobit pols
=#

# Fit the three single-regressor models quietly via chunk-1 helpers
# (logit_stata / probit_stata for the binary-link models, and
# FixedEffectModels.reg for OLS), get fitted probabilities, then
# summarize via `summarize_stata` (chunk 1).
fml_hh    = GLM.@formula(ins ~ hhincome)
logit_hh  = logit_stata(df14, fml_hh; quiet = true)
probit_hh = probit_stata(df14, fml_hh; quiet = true)
ols_hh    = FixedEffectModels.reg(df14, fml_hh)

df14.plogit  = GLM.predict(logit_hh.model)
df14.pprobit = GLM.predict(probit_hh.model)
df14.pols    = FixedEffectModels.predict(ols_hh, df14)

summarize_stata(df14, [:ins, :plogit, :pprobit, :pols]);
```

### 14.6.5 The prvalue command for fitted probabilities

```{julia}
#=
* Fitted probabilities for selected baseline using margins (prvalue no longer available)
quietly logit ins retire $xlist
* Calculate predicted probabilities at specific values
margins, at(age=65 retire=0 hstatusg=1 hhincome=50 educyear=17 married=1 hisp=0)
* Or use margins for marginal effects of hhincome
margins, dydx(hhincome) atmeans
=#
#=
* Fitted probabilities for selected baseline using margins (prvalue no longer available)
quietly logit ins retire $xlist
* Calculate predicted probabilities at specific values
margins, at(age=65 retire=0 hstatusg=1 hhincome=50 educyear=17 married=1 hisp=0)
* Or use margins for marginal effects of hhincome
margins, dydx(hhincome) atmeans
=#

# Fit logit quietly via the chunk-1 helper. Then run two `margins` calls:
#   (1) Adjusted prediction  Pr(ins=1)  at the user-specified point — uses
#       `margins_stata` (chunk 1) with the new `mean_fn = :logit` branch.
#   (2) dy/dx of hhincome at means — uses
#       `margins_dydx_atmeans_binary_stata` (chunk 1) with `link = :logit`.
fml_mar = GLM.@formula(ins ~ retire + age + hstatusg + hhincome +
                              educyear + married + hisp)
mar_fit = logit_stata(df14, fml_mar; quiet = true)
β_mar   = mar_fit.β_glm
V_mar   = mar_fit.V_glm
cn_mar  = mar_fit.coefnames_glm
X_mar   = mar_fit.X_glm
n_mar   = mar_fit.n

# (1) margins, at(age=65 retire=0 hstatusg=1 hhincome=50 educyear=17 married=1 hisp=0)
at_dict = Dict("(Intercept)" => 1.0,
               "retire"      => 0.0,
               "age"         => 65.0,
               "hstatusg"    => 1.0,
               "hhincome"    => 50.0,
               "educyear"    => 17.0,
               "married"     => 1.0,
               "hisp"        => 0.0)
c_at = [at_dict[name] for name in cn_mar]
margins_stata(β_mar, V_mar, X_mar;
              at = c_at,
              at_labels = [:retire => 0, :age => 65, :hstatusg => 1,
                           :hhincome => 50, :educyear => 17,
                           :married => 1, :hisp => 0],
              mean_fn    = :logit,
              vce_label  = "OIM",
              expression = "Pr(ins), predict()")

# (2) margins, dydx(hhincome) atmeans
x̄ = vec(Statistics.mean(X_mar, dims = 1))
idx_hh = findfirst(==("hhincome"), cn_mar)
margins_dydx_atmeans_binary_stata(β_mar, V_mar, x̄, idx_hh;
    link       = :logit,
    var_name   = "hhincome",
    depvar     = "ins",
    vce_label  = "OIM",
    n_obs      = n_mar,
    at_labels  = [n => Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", x̄[i])
                  for (i, n) in enumerate(cn_mar) if n != "(Intercept)"]);
```
